articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 11 Trade Value for This Year's Top 50 NFL Players
articles.summary: Maybe you're like me.
articles.body:
Maybe in one league you have the most points scored but also the most points scored against, and are painfully stuck with a 5-5 record. Maybe in another league you have the fourth most points scored but, AGAIN, the most points scored against and are a devastating 3-7.

Maybe, more than ever, you just need a well-timed trade to salvage the season. Maybe you need to trade from a place of depth to address a need. Maybe there's that gullible player in your league who you might be able to fleece. C'mon, do something .

If you find yourself in that situation, the fantasy trade value chart is here to help. You can't control how many points the other team is going to score, but you can at least put your best foot forward.

Players who would be ranked in the 51-100 range have a trade value between six and two. Players below the top-100 range have a value of one. Trade values are based on PPR scoring, so adjust according to your league's particular scoring settings. May the fantasy points be with you!

For one, some of his touchdown production has regressed to the mean. Williams found the end zone five times in the first five weeks but has reached paydirt just twice since. He was also a far bigger factor in the passing game, with 27 catches through five games and only 11 receptions since. He's seeing about the same amount of carries overall, but Blake Corum has gone from nine touches a game between Weeks 1-5 to 14.2 touches per contest in the last five games.

And now it's Corum that's finding the end zone, with five scores in the past five games. This, obviously, is a huge concern to anybody rostering Williams. Plus, with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams out injured, the Rams have begun to experiment with both players on the field at the same time.

Not to mention Ronnie Rivers entering the picture in Week 10:

Because Williams still ranks top-10 in overall points at the running back position, you might be able to sell on him relatively high. You may want to consider doing so—at best, he's back in close-to-evenly split platoon. At worst, Corum will continue getting the goal-line looks and enough love in the passing game to limit Williams' receptions. This situation is trending poorly for Williams and positively for Corum.

articles.title: Biggest Sleepers at Every Position for Week 11 Fantasy Football 2026
articles.summary: In Week 11, six NFL teams are on a bye, so most fantasy football managers are hunting for sleepers and streamers to fuel a playoff run or lock up top seeds in their leagues.
articles.body:
In Week 11, six NFL teams are on a bye, so most fantasy football managers are hunting for sleepers and streamers to fuel a playoff run or lock up top seeds in their leagues.

If you're searching the free-agent pool, this week's sleeper list can lead you in the right direction.

Even though Thursday night's game features two three-win teams, there's a fantasy gem at running back who's growing into a solid role.

A Tennessee Titans quarterback-receiver stack could rack up big numbers in a potential high-scoring matchup.

Lastly, keep an eye on a couple of pass-catchers in an AFC West showdown between the Denver Broncos and the Las Vegas Raiders.

Here are the biggest sleepers at each position for Week 11. All selections below are available in at least 50 percent of leagues, according to FantasyPros' consensus roster percentages.

QB Aaron Rodgers at Philadelphia Eagles (45 Percent Rostered)

The Pittsburgh Steelers may have reinforcements for their matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

They opened the 21-day practice windows for wideouts Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger), giving both a chance to return from injured reserve. While neither is guaranteed to suit up on Sunday, Wilson went through a full practice, and Pittman logged a limited session.

Furthermore, the Philadelphia Eagles allow the ninth-most fantasy points to quarterbacks.

Aaron Rodgers' completion rate dipped below 53 percent in his last two outings, but his efficiency could trend back in the right direction with help at receiver potentially on the way in an advantageous matchup.

Rodgers threw three touchdown passes in each of three consecutive games from Weeks 3 through 5, with Wilson leading the Steelers in receiving yards in two of those contests. The 42-year-old signal-caller could have another strong outing if his receiving corps is closer to full strength.

QB Cam Ward at Dallas Cowboys (17 Percent Rostered)

Cam Ward is starting to make strides, throwing for 535 yards, four touchdowns and an interception over the last two weeks, completing at least 65 percent of his passes in both outings.

This week, Ward draws a favorable matchup against the Dallas Cowboys, who give up the third-most fantasy points to quarterbacks and rank 26th in passing yards allowed.

The Cowboys stripped defensive coordinator Christian Parker of his play-calling duties and reassigned them to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine, but that move won't fix the Cowboys' defense overnight.

Ward won't have wideout Wan'Dale Robinson, who will miss the rest of the season with an ankle injury, but Carnell Tate started the week with limited practice after missing two games with a shoulder injury.

The Titans could heavily target Tate and running back Tony Pollard, who's facing his former team for the first time, in a high-scoring matchup. If Tennessee falls behind, Ward would still need to throw a high volume of passes on a negative game script.

RB Kaelon Black vs. Minnesota Vikings (40 Percent Rostered)

This is probably your last chance to add Kaelon Black before he eclipses the 50 percent rostered threshold. The rookie third-rounder has logged at least 11 carries in three straight games, scoring in two.

Despite two fumbles, Black has carved out a decent role in the San Francisco 49ers backfield alongside star running back Christian McCaffrey. He's seen only eight targets in the passing game, but his workload on the ground puts him on the fantasy radar.

Although Minnesota has surrendered just five rushing touchdowns in nine games, its defense has shown some vulnerability against the run, allowing 134-plus yards in three of the last four weeks. Ollie Gordon II, Jahmyr Gibbs and James Cook III all ran for 100-plus yards against the Vikings. Colts ball-carriers Jonathan Taylor and Seth McGowan combined for 141 yards and a touchdown against this unit.

McCaffrey and Black could see a big workload if the 49ers focus on attacking the Vikings' 17th-ranked run defense rather than their second-ranked pass defense.

RB Seth McGowan at Houston Texans (24 Percent Rostered)

If you're looking for a quick start to the week, consider Seth McGowan as a flex option for Thursday night.

The 25-year-old has been efficient while seeing more touches. He's averaged 5.8 yards or more per carry in four of his last five games and scored touchdowns in consecutive contests.

In Week 10, McGowan logged 12 carries for 77 yards and a touchdown against the Miami Dolphins, narrowly outscoring Taylor 13.7–12.3 in PPR formats.

Given the Houston Texans' defensive struggles this season, the Colts could make this a competitive matchup, allowing them to feature their running backs. If McGowan gets 10-12 touches at his current efficiency, he's a solid pickup for this week and the rest of the season.

WR Pat Bryant vs. Las Vegas Raiders (13 Percent Rostered)

In his first game back from injured reserve, Pat Bryant caught four passes for 56 yards and a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers in Week 9. In five games, he's shown the ability to make explosive plays, averaging 14.5 yards per catch.

Even though Denver's lead wide receiver, Jaylen Waddle, is likely to return to action after leaving the team's previous game with a concussion, Bryant could still feast on the Las Vegas Raiders' 23rd-ranked pass defense, which has allowed 22 passing touchdowns in 10 games.

Moreover, Las Vegas is allowing the seventh-most fantasy points to wideouts, so Denver could have two fantasy-relevant players at the position. Also, keep in mind that quarterback Bo Nix has thrown two touchdown passes in consecutive outings.

If the Broncos attack the Raiders through the air, Bryant could post his best fantasy stat line of the season.

WR Elic Ayomanor at Dallas Cowboys (12 Percent Rostered)

Entering Week 11, Wan'Dale Robinson leads the Tennessee Titans' pass-catching group with 54 targets. Tennessee placed him on injured reserve, so there should be plenty of targets to go around.

Last week, Elic Ayomanor had his most productive game of the season, hauling in five of his 10 targets for 79 yards. Even if rookie first-rounder Carnell Tate returns from injury, Ayomanor will likely see enough targets to be a solid WR2 in a favorable matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

The Cowboys allow the fifth-most fantasy points to wide receivers, and they've surrendered 19 passing touchdowns in 10 games. Also, FanDuel has set the total at 54.5 points for this contest. So this could be a scoring shootout between two bottom-seven pass defenses.

Ayomanor isn't a flashy name, but based on the matchup and potential game script, he's in one of the best fantasy situations for a wide receiver.

TE Chig Okonkwo vs. Cincinnati Bengals (28 Percent Rostered)

Given wide receiver Terry McLaurin's season-ending knee injury, Chig Okonkwo should be rostered in more leagues. Since McLaurin went down in Week 6, Okonkwo has played a steady role in Washington's passing attack.

In three of the Commanders' previous four games, Okonkwo has seen at least seven targets. He's also racked up 57 or more receiving yards in three of his last five outings.

This week, Okonkwo gets a plus matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals, who allow the ninth-most fantasy points to tight ends.

Even in dominant wins over the Atlanta Falcons and Pittsburgh Steelers, Cincinnati gave up touchdowns to tight ends Charlie Woerner and Pat Freiermuth. Before those games, the Bengals allowed Tennessee Titans tight ends Gunnar Helm and Daniel Bellinger to rack up 112 combined receiving yards.

As a secondary target behind lead wide receiver Stefon Diggs, Okonkwo has a path to be a low-end TE1 in this week's Monday night matchup.

TE Michael Mayer at Denver Broncos (26 Percent Rostered)

As of Thursday, Las Vegas Raiders All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers is questionable at best to suit up against the Denver Broncos. He exited last week's game against the Seattle Seahawks with an ankle injury.

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Bowers avoided a serious issue, but his injury is still "significant."

Without Bowers, rookie Fernando Mendoza will need a big-bodied safety blanket in the passing game. The first-year signal-caller didn't get much help from his wide receiver corps last week. Jack Bech was the only Raiders wideout to log multiple catches (two) in Mendoza's debut.

Entering Week 11, tight end Michael Mayer is third among Raiders pass-catchers in receptions (41) with 404 yards and a touchdown. He'll take on a bigger role if Bowers is sidelined. That said, Mayer has seen a steady volume of targets as the primary inline tight end while Bowers has lined up on the perimeter.

The Broncos allow the third-most fantasy points to tight ends, so Mayer has a decent floor of production with or without Bowers on the field Sunday. If Mendoza has to play catchup, look for him to throw between the hashes rather than test two-time All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II and budding fourth-year cover man Riley Moss on the outside.

Fantasy points allowed statistics are provided by FantasyPros .

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Tennessee DL Xavier Gilliam
articles.summary: Xavier Gilliam is the biggest riser in the defensive tackle class, bursting onto the scene with a very impressive performance during the 2026 season. He combines quickness, athleticism, and strength to be a very good gap-shooter and interior pass rusher in the NFL.
articles.body:
Xavier Gilliam is the biggest riser in the defensive tackle class, bursting onto the scene with a very impressive performance during the 2026 season. He combines quickness, athleticism, and strength to be a very good gap-shooter and interior pass rusher in the NFL.

A 3-star recruit in the 2024 high school class, Gilliam's college career began at Penn State. He redshirted as a true freshman and was a rotational player the following year, collecting 15 tackles, two tackles for loss and half a sack for the Nittany Lions.

That's why the Maryland native has been such a big riser; he was an unknown commodity before transferring to Tennessee and having a dominant campaign this fall.

Matt Holder has been a part of B/R's Scouting Department for five seasons. He also writes about the Las Vegas Raiders and NFL draft for SB Nation's Silver and Black Pride , and co-hosts a YouTube Channel, Tape Don't Lie , providing film breakdowns and more draft prospect analysis.

Gilliam has a very good get-off with a quick reaction to the snap and very good acceleration off the line of scrimmage. That lets him shoot gaps, get penetration, or pressure interior offensive linemen with speed around the edge, leading to oversets.

Sets up his pass-rush moves by stemming inside or outside and has the quickness and agility to win in the opposite direction.

Has shown a handful of moves he can win with (arm over, cross-chop and rip), and has the hip fluidity to get clean wins around the edges.

Quickness allows him to beat offensive linemen across their faces.

As a power rusher, he has a decent long-arm move to get linemen off his body and is solid at engaging with the bull rush before using his agility and quickness to get on an edge and escape.

Effective in line games, he's physical and attacks the inside shoulder as the penetrator on stunts and has the lateral movement skills to take efficient paths to the quarterback as the looper.

Rushes with a plan, constantly working counter moves if he doesn't win initially, and has a high motor.

Can win as a pass-rusher from multiple alignments, Tennessee played him anywhere from a nose tackle to on the edge.

When he shoots his hands as a run defender, he has plenty of upper body strength to gain control of the block.

Runs his feet and has good agility to avoid getting reached or scooped.

Good at sinking his hips to anchor and fight back against pressure when slanting.

Gilliam is a little undersized for an NFL defensive tackle, lacking the ideal height for the position.

Pad level rises when rushing the passer, making it difficult to collapse the pocket with a pure bull rush.

Against the run, he can get caught with late and wide hand placement, exposing his chest and making it difficult ot get extension on blocks.

Lacks some sand in his pants to hold his gap against double teams and combo blocks.

PLAY-STYLE ARCHETYPE : One-gap penetrating DT (Byron Murphy II to Kobie Turner)

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for South Carolina QB LaNorris Sellers
articles.summary: LaNorris Sellers has an outstanding physical toolset that could develop into a game-changing quarterback.
articles.body:
LaNorris Sellers has an outstanding physical toolset that could develop into a game-changing quarterback.

The South Florence native is a physical, dynamic rushing threat that defenses must account for. He will hurt defenses as an improvisational scrambler or on designed quarterback runs.

Sellers is a former 4-star recruit in the 2023 class. This is his third year as the Gamecocks' full-time starter, and he has over 20 games under his belt. Sellers has immense developmental upside that should entice NFL decision-makers searching for a franchise quarterback.

Dame is the lead host of the Locked On NFL Draft podcast. Previously, he spent three years as a senior draft analyst for The Draft Network while evaluating draft prospects as the founder of The Scouting Room .

Sellers has a very strong arm to power the football into tight windows and push it vertically.

Can move the launch point by design or throw on the move if pressure flushes him out of the pocket. Keeps his eyes downfield.

He has excellent open-field speed; he can burn defenders for long, explosive runs and convert third downs.

He is making strides in processing and working through his progressions with timing.

Big, strong frame inside the pocket to shrug off/fight through contact to avoid sacks.

Footwork and balance as a passer in the pocket are improving.

Sellers suffers from a "hero ball" mentality, where he refuses to allow plays to die, leading to turnover-worthy plays.

He lacks consistency throwing with anticipation; more of a see-it-throw-it quarterback.

Inconsistent ball placement and location.

Would benefit from adding more eye manipulation to hold and move defenders in coverage.

Play Style Family : LaNorris Sellers brings a dynamic dual-threat at quarterback. He is showcasing flashes of game-changing ability as both a passer and a runner. Sellers has a big, strong frame and high-end traits, with an equally high ceiling. Similar to Daunte Culpepper, he's big, fast, and strong, with immense arm talent under center.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Alabama CB Zabien Brown
articles.summary: Zabien Brown consistently rises to the biggest moments against top competition when he steps onto the field. If it's fourth down and your defense needs a player to shut down, he'll get the job done more often than not. He's great in off coverage, letting his eyes take him to the football in both phases, and he values willingness against the run. Brown was named a captain for Alabama's football team in 2026, and he leads their defense with his attitude and physicality.
articles.body:
Zabien Brown consistently rises to the biggest moments against top competition when he steps onto the field. If it's fourth down and your defense needs a player to shut down, he'll get the job done more often than not. He's great in off coverage, letting his eyes take him to the football in both phases, and he values willingness against the run. Brown was named a captain for Alabama's football team in 2026, and he leads their defense with his attitude and physicality.

He's played his entire career for the Crimson Tide as a 5- star recruit and has continued to develop his technique as a cornerback in this defense. If Brown declares, he should expect to be selected on day one of the NFL Draft in April, as he continues to showcase his talents among the best teams in the country.

Dan has covered the Kansas City Chiefs and the NFL Draft since 2019 while contributing for RGR Football. Most recently, he spent the 2025 draft cycle at The Draft Network and is entering his first season in our scouting department.

Brown showcases unique eye discipline and consistently identifies run concepts and route combinations.

Excels at reading and reacting in zone or off coverage with good depth and a quick trigger downhill.

An above-average athlete, he plays with controlled movements at all levels of the field and can decelerate to match receivers at the top of routes.

He's a competitive player in the run game, and that translates down the field at the catch point against receivers.

His instincts show up in coverage and when the ball is in the air, with a great ability to locate the football.

Brown will get walked down in man coverage, creating too much space for receivers inside to access.

Needs to improve his patience against release packages in man coverage and trust his athletic ability.

Inconsistencies in tackling technique lead to yards after the catch that need to be cleaned up.

Recovery speed when stacked vertically appears to be average, which limits his press-coverage use.

PLAYSTYLE FAMILY : Jaylon Johnson profile with ideal size and zone match instincts.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Cal S Kingston Lopa
articles.summary: Players who find themselves around the football are highly coveted by the NFL, and Kingston Lopa, in his first season as a starter, has often found himself in that position. A natural feel for space and the ability to read the quarterback's eyes are gifts. He's using those gifts to make opposing offenses pay every time he steps foot on the field.
articles.body:
Players who find themselves around the football are highly coveted by the NFL, and Kingston Lopa, in his first season as a starter, has often found himself in that position. A natural feel for space and the ability to read the quarterback's eyes are gifts. He's using those gifts to make opposing offenses pay every time he steps foot on the field.

An inexperienced player for Cal, the former 4-star recruit transferred from Oregon after making minimal impact in his two seasons as a Duck and immediately started on the Golden Bears' defense. Lopa has been a playmaker from the jump, and it's hard not to see the "Kyle Hamilton mold" when watching him play with his body type .

Dan has covered the Kansas City Chiefs and the NFL Draft since 2019 while contributing for RGR Football. Most recently, he spent the 2025 draft cycle at The Draft Network and is entering his first season in our scouting department.

Lopa plays with an aggressive, downhill mindset paired with a natural ability to read out plays quickly to create chaos.

He has natural field instincts and mirrors the quarterback at a high level to take away route options and the football.

A great mover in space, Lopa can read and react smoothly in zone and has the coverage tools to play man coverage against tight ends.

He gets downhill in a hurry, which makes him an asset in filling lanes against the run quickly.

The 6'5", 210-pound safety will thrive in a cover 3-based defense where he can fill lanes consistently from depth and take away routes over the middle.

Lopa is an overly aggressive player, which leads to missed tackles and big plays on the back of it.

His true range is a question, which makes living on top of a defense limited for him.

He is an inexperienced player playing on many natural gifts. His Rolodex needs filling to grow his football IQ.

Tackling technique is a work in progress as he falls off too many tackles.

PLAYSTYLE FAMILY : Kyle Hamilton coded with a slighter build.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Ohio State Edge Kenyatta Jackson
articles.summary: Kenyatta Jackson is a physically imposing edge defender who has added some versatility to his game during the 2026 season. The 6'3", 263-pound Ohio State product was on the 2026 NFL draft radar and has elevated his stock by showing improved athleticism this year. However, he still isn't in the elite tier of athletes for the position.
articles.body:
Kenyatta Jackson is a physically imposing edge defender who has added some versatility to his game during the 2026 season. The 6'3", 263-pound Ohio State product was on the 2026 NFL draft radar and has elevated his stock by showing improved athleticism this year. However, he still isn't in the elite tier of athletes for the position.

A 4-star recruit in the 2022 class, Jackson didn't see the field much until his junior season. He was a backup behind JT Tuimoloau (the Colts' 2025 second-round pick) and Jack Sawyer (the Steelers' 2025 fourth-round pick), recording 16 tackles, three tackles for loss, and 1.5 sacks that year.

The 2025 campaign was the Miami Gardens, Fla. native's breakout performance, serving as a starter and logging 27 tackles, 11 TFLs, 6.5 sacks, and two passes defended. That was good enough to earn honorable mention All-Big Ten honors.

Matt Holder has been a part of B/R's Scouting Department for five seasons. He also writes about the Las Vegas Raiders and NFL draft for SB Nation's Silver and Black Pride , and co-hosts a YouTube Channel, Tape Don't Lie , providing film breakdowns and more draft prospect analysis.

Jackson has good size and a good frame for an NFL edge defender. He also has 34-inch arms, according to The Athletic's Dane Brugler .

Looks like he put on some good weight in the 2026 offseason, thickening up his lower half.

Against the run, he takes on blocks with a low pad level and a wide base, and has good strength and physicality at the point of attack. He also plays with his hands in front of him and uses them to engage offensive linemen.

Can set the edge and hold his ground against one-on-one blocks from offensive linemen or when taking on pullers.

Decent hump and arm-over moves to catch offensive linemen leaning and escape blocks.

As a pass-rusher, he has solid power and keeps his legs moving through contact to occasionally collapse the pocket against offensive tackles. Also, he has the strength to push through the tackle's inside shoulder.

Has flashed arm-over and cross-chop moves as decent secondary pass-rush moves.

Lateral movement skills have improved in 2026 to potentially win across offensive linemen's faces as a pass-rusher.

Good pass-rush motor and works counter moves if he doesn't win immediately.

Jackson still has room for growth as an overall athlete when it comes to his fluidity and quickness to be able to win with finesse moves around the edge more consistently at the next level.

Not explosive off the line of scrimmage to threaten offensive tackles with speed.

Could afford to work the hands more after contact as a pass-rusher.

Subpar bend to turn tight corners at the top of the rush.

Slow to recognize reach blocks and lacks rotational strength to keep his shoulders square, leading to him getting reached/scooped out of his gap.

Hand placement when taking on blocks is a little wide, exposing his chest a bit and preventing him from maximizing his extension.

Not strong enough to hold his gap against double teams and combo blocks from offensive tackles and tight ends when playing as a 4i-technique. Profiles better as a base end in even fronts.

PLAY-STYLE ARCHETYPE : Base End (Alex Wright to Emmanuel Ogbah)

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Alabama DL Devan Thompkins
articles.summary: Devan Thompkins has always been a rare and unique athlete for his size. After transferring from USC to Alabama this season, the 6'5", 300-pound defensive lineman is just starting to reach his potential. He has the movement skills and strength to be an impactful every-down player in the NFL.
articles.body:
Devan Thompkins has always been a rare and unique athlete for his size. After transferring from USC to Alabama this season, the 6'5", 300-pound defensive lineman is just starting to reach his potential. He has the movement skills and strength to be an impactful every-down player in the NFL.

A 3-star recruit in the 2022 high school class, Thompkins spent four years with the Trojans. He played in 27 games with 17 starts, collecting 56 tackles, nine tackles for loss, 4.5 sacks and five passes defended.

Matt Holder has been a part of B/R's Scouting Department for five seasons. He also writes about the Las Vegas Raiders and NFL draft for SB Nation's Silver and Black Pride , and co-hosts a YouTube Channel, Tape Don't Lie , providing film breakdowns and more draft prospect analysis.

Thompkins has good size for an NFL "big end" (4i- to 5-technique) and appears to have long arms.

Basketball background -- didn't play football in high school until he transferred schools his senior year -- which shows up in his movement skills, possessing good burst, agility and quickness to be a good overall athlete.

Good get-off/acceleration off the line of scrimmage to be effective at pushing the pocket when bull rushing or turning speed to power, especially with his strength and length.

Decent rip move as a pass-rusher that he can use to win around the edge occassionally.

Against the run, he has the upper body strength to gain control of the block and set the edge against offensive tackles when he gets his hands up quickly.

Strength and length allow him to get extension on blocks.

Quick to recognize reach blocks and has the agility to run his feet and avoid getting reached.

Position and scheme versatility, showing the ability to play anywhere from a 3- to a 5-technique.

Thompkins plays with high pad level, which makes it difficult for him to anchor and stay in his gap against combo blocks/double teams.

Can be slow to get his hands up against the run or have wide hand placement, exposing his chest to offensive linemen.

Gap control is occassionally an issue; he has a habit of working around blocks/vacating his assignment or taking on blocks square and guessing where the running back is going instead of shading in his gap and reacting to the back.

As a pass-rusher, he can get caught doing too much dancing during the stem phase of the rush instead of using his get-off and strength to just win with power.

Needs to improve his hand usage to expand his pass-rush arsenal.

Also, can afford to be better at working the offensive lineman's hands after contact and rushing with a plan to execute counter moves.

PLAY-STYLE ARCHETYPE : Scheme versatile "big end" (Christian Barmore to Adetomiwa Adebawore)

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Notre Dame Edge Boubacar Traore
articles.summary: Boubacar Traore is an eye-popping edge rusher and a very good athlete with a nasty spin move that will help him be a productive pass rusher in the NFL. He also shows some nuance by setting up his moves and using his hands to win around the edge.
articles.body:
Boubacar Traore is an eye-popping edge rusher and a very good athlete with a nasty spin move that will help him be a productive pass rusher in the NFL. He also shows some nuance by setting up his moves and using his hands to win around the edge.

However, the 6'5", 253-pound edge falls into the "just another guy" category against the run, to the point where Notre Dame would often take him out of the game in run situations.

A 4-star recruit in the 2023 high school class, the Golden Domer didn't see the field much until his sophomore season. Unfortunately, a torn ACL limited him to five games, 11 tackles, five tackles for loss and three sacks. Traore had solid production in 2025 with 37 tackles, 10 TFLs and 6.5 sacks.

Matt Holder has been a part of B/R's Scouting Department for five seasons. He also writes about the Las Vegas Raiders and NFL draft for SB Nation's Silver and Black Pride , and co-hosts a YouTube Channel, Tape Don't Lie , providing film breakdowns and more draft prospect analysis.

Traore is a high-level athlete who is quick and has very good lateral movement skills to win across offensive tackles' faces.

Good frame and size for an NFL edge defender, and appears to have long arms.

Sets up his pass rush moves well by stemming inside and using his quickness to win outside or vice versa, and by combining his moves with a euro step.

Has a very good spin move, showing impressive quickness to test offensive tackles' change-of-direction skills, and a good ice pick to clear their hands.

Also shows a good cross-chop and active hands as a pass-rusher, and is decent at turning speed into power.

Flexible in his lower half to bend and corner at the top of the rush.

Strong enough to take on and defeat blocks from smaller tight ends.

Traore doesn't make much of an impact as a run defender and was often taken out of the game on run downs. Didn't even play against Navy in 2025 with Navy's run-heavy/option offense.

Not very physical when taking on blocks in the running.

Lack the strength to get extension and escape blocks from offensive tackles. Also, doesn't have the rotational strength to keep his shoulders square when taking on reach blocks.

Poor instincts against the run; he struggles to diagnose play design/blocking schemes and/or locate the ball in the backfield.

Also will leave his gap early, creating rushing lanes.

For as fast and athletic as he is, his burst off the line of scrimmage leaves something to be desired.

PLAY-STYLE ARCHETYPE : Pass-Rush Specialist (Odafe Oweh to Joseph Ossai)

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Georgia S KJ Bolden
articles.summary: It doesn't matter how big KJ Bolden is; he'll hit whoever comes his way, and you'll feel it. Such a physical player, and for an "undersized" defender, he plays with the big boys. Whether it's a receiver crossing the field trying to make the catch or a runner in open space, Bolden lines up hits with the best and makes his presence felt.
articles.body:
It doesn't matter how big KJ Bolden is; he'll hit whoever comes his way, and you'll feel it. Such a physical player, and for an "undersized" defender, he plays with the big boys. Whether it's a receiver crossing the field trying to make the catch or a runner in open space, Bolden lines up hits with the best and makes his presence felt.

The former 5- star recruit has been a mainstay since he stepped on the field for the Bulldogs' defense and has a natural flair for football. He knows the type of game he wants to play, and if you're not ready to meet him, it won't end well for the ball carrier.

Bolden is looking to follow in former teammate Malaki Starks' footsteps and be a first-round selection in 2027. Doing that at the safety spot isn't an easy task in many years, but he has the tools to make it happen.

Dan has covered the Kansas City Chiefs and the NFL Draft since 2019 while contributing for RGR Football. Most recently, he spent the 2025 draft cycle at The Draft Network and is entering his first season in our scouting department.

Bolden is the ultimate tone setter for the defense; laying the wood all day long to the opposing offense.

He has a nose for the football and route combinations underneath, making it easy for him to trigger on throws and limit yards after the catch.

He's a menace against the run and triggering downhill in any capacity. Quick to recognize and quicker to get involved.

A reactive player at heart, he reads the quarterback's eyes and ties them to unfolding routes to get a jump on the throw.

An excellent tackler at all levels of the field, which is especially important as the last line of defense on the backend.

Bolden will rely on the eyes of the quarterback too often and can lose developing routes as they get further downfield, opening up big plays.

His size will limit him against larger tight ends and receivers, particularly at the catch point.

The 6'0" 195-pound safety will take overly aggressive paths to the football from a deep alignment that leads to missed opportunities.

PLAYER ARCHETYPE : In the Brian Branch Family of hard-nosed safeties. He does his best work around the line of scrimmage and triggering on intermediate throws.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Virginia Tech TE Luke Reynolds
articles.summary: Luke Reynolds is the biggest breakout tight end of this class and has done it with insane ball tracking and body control. He catches nearly everything thrown at him and then makes defenders miss in space at a high level.
articles.body:
Luke Reynolds is the biggest breakout tight end of this class and has done it with insane ball tracking and body control. He catches nearly everything thrown at him and then makes defenders miss in space at a high level.

He left a talented tight end room at Penn State to follow James Franklin in his return to Virginia Tech, not just to be with the coach who recruited him, but to be "the guy." Reynolds hasn't disappointed and has taken every opportunity to showcase his talents.

The former 5- star recruit bet on himself, and it paid off big as he rose through the tight end ranks in college football. He's a high-effort player, which pays off in the run and passing game, and he's the type of player NFL coaches will love.

Dan has covered the Kansas City Chiefs and the NFL Draft since 2019 while contributing for RGR Football. Most recently, he spent the 2025 draft cycle at The Draft Network and is entering his first season in our scouting department.

Reynolds showcases incredibly reliable hands at every level of the field and his ball tracking works in tandem to make that easier.

Get him the ball in space and let him work. He has a great feel for space and quick movements that make defenders miss and maximize YAC.

The 6'4", 250-pound tight end can be utilized in a multitude of ways as a receiver to create one-on-ones to exploit with high-end ball skills.

He's a growing route runner with excellent manipulation tactics at the top of routes and intention-based tools.

Blocking down and on the move highlight his effort and ability in the run game to open lanes.

Reynolds needs to continue developing his hand usage in his route stem to fight through physical man coverage and stay on target.

He will need to improve his point of attack angles and timing to not fall off blocks and improve his utility as an in-line blocker.

Locating soft spots in zone quickly pre-snap will earn him even more targets, not just as a schemed-up playmaker.

PLAYER ARCHETYPE : Mark Andrews-type tight end. Can realistically do much of what an offense asks of him while remaining a highly reliable receiver.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Oklahoma DL David Stone
articles.summary: Using a first-round pick on David Stone is a gamble, but he has elite traits that are worth betting on. articles.body:
Using a first-round pick on David Stone is a gamble, but he has elite traits that are worth betting on. The 6'3", 315-pound defensive tackle's technique is a work in progress in both phases of the game, but prospects with his combination of size, strength, athleticism, and quickness don't come around very often.

A 5-star recruit and the No. 9 overall player in the 2024 high school class, Stone participated in every game as a true freshman, but sparingly. Despite making just two starts during his sophomore year, he was part of the Sooners' defensive line rotation and racked up 42 tackles, eight for loss and 1.5 sacks in 13 games.

Matt Holder has been a part of B/R's Scouting Department for five seasons. He also writes about the Las Vegas Raiders and NFL draft for SB Nation's Silver and Black Pride , and co-hosts a YouTube Channel, Tape Don't Lie , providing film breakdowns and more draft prospect analysis.

Stone has good size for an NFL defensive tackle and moves very well with impressive acceleration, agility and quickness.

Quick to react to the snap and has good burst off the line to get penetration when gap shooting. Also has a solid rip move to fight through contact when penetrating.

Plenty of strength at the point of attack and has nearly 35-inch arms, according to 247Sports' Andrew Irvins , to get plenty of extension on blocks and reset the line of scrimmage.

Can make tackles with offensive linemen hanging onto him.

Athleticism gives him upside as a pass rusher if he learns how to use his hands and loosens up his hips.

Agile to be an effective looper on line games.

Offers some alignment versatility with experience playing anywhere from a 4i-technique to nose tackle.

Stone doesn't have much starting experience heading into the 2026 season and has underwhelming pass-rush production with 2.5 sacks in 2024 and 2025 combined.

A little slow to get his hands up in both phases of the game, making it difficult to consistently take advantage of his strength and length at the point of attack.

Plays with high pad level, hurting the effectiveness of his bull rush.

Isn't good at working the offensive lineman's hands and shows some hip tightness, making it difficult to work the edges as a pass-rusher.

Doesn't rush with a plan; rarely throws counter moves if he doesn't win initially.

Subpar gap integrity; he will get set up by running backs and vacate his gap before the back commits, opening up a rushing lane.

Will miss sacks or TFLs because he struggles to break down in the backfield and ends up overrunning quarterbacks or running backs.

PLAY-STYLE ARCHETYPE : Versatile and high-variance interior defender (Nnamdi Madubuike to Mazi Smith)

articles.body: Quinnen Williams has been with the Dallas Cowboys since 2025 - the same time Jerry Jones promoted offensive coordinator Brian Schottenheimer the head coach for the Cowboys.Anyhow, Williams now represents Dallas, and he speaks for them, and whatever he says may affect the Cowboys. So, what does the defensive tackle do? He adopts the famous Jerry-speak! Dallas media and fans have reportedly often pointed out Jerry-speak whenever they see it.An executive reportedly told The Washington Post that Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones mixes plain-spoken country with theatricality. When he talks in colorful metaphors or long stories during press conferences, it isn’t because he has lost his train of thought- it could be a deliberate move to avoid hard questions without looking evasive.The same thought process was probably adopted by Jones’ current defensive tackle - Quinnen Williams. Just that Williams did not make reporters get lost in long metaphors or colorful stories but kept it simple: “I’m gonna keep that to myself.”Quinnen Williams’ secretive style of dodging Dallas Cowboys’ defense questionsIt’s midseason - the defensive tackle clearly does not want his defensive play-calling story to get out. Or maybe Quinnen Williams doesn’t want to comment on it because he wasn’t happy about it. Or maybe he was happy about it but was told not to say anything. It could be anything.His one-line comment repeated 12 times - for 12 questions which he intently listened to - as though contemplating his replies in his head - but what came out of his mouth? That one line repeated 12 times! - “I’m gonna keep that to myself.” It could also mean he has a lot to say about the change, but he was advised to keep his views to himself!The players-only defensive meeting was meant for him and his teammates alone; he doesn’t wish to leak those details to the media or other teams. The reason behind his repetitive reply could be practically anything.Anyhow. Hats off to the reporters who kept pressing for more answers. Especially now, when the playcalling duties of Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker have changed; they will now be in the hands of Mike Pettine, a senior defensive assistant.As per Off Day Chatter’s Pete Altomaro, the four-time Pro Bowler did have a few more sentences about the defensive playcalling shakeup than that repetitive cassette - “Everything is on us. We’re on the field no matter what play gets called, no matter who calls it, we’ve got to execute the play - and that’s what we haven’t been doing; we’ve got to do it going forward.”Christian Parker robbed of playcalling duties due to Cowboys’ struggling defense“I want to clarify, right off the bat, that Christian Parker is still our defensive coordinator; he’s a critical piece of what we’re trying to do as we search for answers and solutions,” head coach Brian Schottenheimer said. “And I think he has an incredibly bright future, not just this year, but beyond it with us.”So the Dallas Cowboys probably want to keep Parker but not fire him. So they want to keep him but rob him of his duties because the Cowboys’ defense ranks last in the 2026 NFL season through Week 10. Total defense rank - 32nd, rush defense rank - 32nd, pass defense rank - 26th, and scoring defense rank - 30th.The Cowboys occupy the second spot in the NFC East at the moment with a 4-6 record - just behind the New York Giants, who have a 5-3-1 record - despite losing their quarterback - Jaxson Dart to a season-ending knee surgery.Anyhow, Dak Prescott and company have an upcoming Week 11 matchup vs. the Tennessee Titans to prove that their defense can still become a threat - that is, after Mike Pettine shows his magic! Otherwise, Quennin Williams’ one-sentence reply repeated 12 times would mean nothing! All that secrecy, all that drama, all that Jerry Jones-mimicking - would be for what then?Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Missouri OT Cayden Green
articles.summary: Cayden Green is a broad, powerful tackle with very good play strength, legitimate NFL size and enough functional athletic ability to remain viable on the edge. His mass, length and anchor allow him to absorb force, close space and impose himself on smaller defenders, while improved flashes of hand usage and processing give him multiple ways to survive in pass protection. Average lateral quickness and inconsistent body control still create volatility against speed, and a move to guard could ultimately maximize his physicality and give him his best long-term NFL fit.
articles.body:
Cayden Green is a broad, powerful tackle with very good play strength, legitimate NFL size and enough functional athletic ability to remain viable on the edge. His mass, length and anchor allow him to absorb force, close space and impose himself on smaller defenders, while improved flashes of hand usage and processing give him multiple ways to survive in pass protection. Average lateral quickness and inconsistent body control still create volatility against speed, and a move to guard could ultimately maximize his physicality and give him his best long-term NFL fit.

Green is a 6'5", 324-pound offensive line prospect who entered Oklahoma as a 4-star recruit in the 2023 class. He appeared in 11 games with five starts at left guard as a true freshman before transferring to Missouri, where he started all 13 games at left guard in 2024. Green moved to left tackle shortly before the 2025 season and made 11 starts there, missing two games due to injury, before returning as Missouri's starting left tackle in 2026.

Brandon is the author of the Trench Warfare newsletter , which focuses exclusively on offensive and defensive line evaluation. He also contributes as an analyst to Establish the Run , serves as the scouting coordinator for OL Masterminds and is a selection committee member for the Joe Moore Award .

Broad, stout frame with very good play strength and enough length to create a large blocking surface. He can absorb force, root his base, and stifle defenders once he gets square and connected.

Particularly effective when he closes space and turns the rep into a physical confrontation. His size and hand strength allow him to engulf lighter edge defenders, step on their toes, and generate displacement on kickouts and angle-drive blocks.

Sturdy anchor with the ability to recover after absorbing an initial surge. He can throw his hips back, reestablish his base, and grind down speed-to-power even when the anchor arrives slightly late.

Functional athletic ability for tackle, with flashes of good processing and hand usage. He can execute vertical and angled sets, carry drag-hand presence through games, and show the awareness to pass off basic line games effectively.

Lateral quickness and high-side range are adequate rather than high-end. His feet can stick after the initial kick, allowing speed rushers to access his upfield shoulder and capture the corner.

Body control remains inconsistent when the picture changes. He will open his hips prematurely, get flat-footed or overextend when his initial strike misses, leaving him vulnerable to swipes, sheds and inside redirection.

Hand placement and sustain can still become sloppy. His physical dimensions allow him to survive imperfect fits, but better synchronization between his hands, feet and hips would create more consistent control rather than forcing him to recover.

PLAYER ARCHETYPE : Powerful, broad-framed starting OT with very good play strength and functional range whose physical traits provide tackle viability, though guard may offer his best long-term NFL fit.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Stanford OT Niki Prongos
articles.summary: Niki Prongos is a long, twitchy tackle with good athletic ability, quick hands, and the range to remain viable on the edge. His movement skills, strike timing, and ability to play long give him developmental starter upside, but inconsistent play strength and hand placement still leave him in too many compromised positions against power and counters. Prongos projects as a developmental tackle whose ceiling depends on becoming more disciplined with his hands and more stable through contact.
articles.body:
Niki Prongos is a long, twitchy tackle with good athletic ability, quick hands, and the range to remain viable on the edge. His movement skills, strike timing, and ability to play long give him developmental starter upside, but inconsistent play strength and hand placement still leave him in too many compromised positions against power and counters. Prongos projects as a developmental tackle whose ceiling depends on becoming more disciplined with his hands and more stable through contact.

Prongos is a 6'7", 315-pound offensive line prospect who entered UCLA as an unranked recruit in the 2022 class. He did not begin playing football until his senior year of high school and appeared in only three games that season due to injury. Prongos started eight games at UCLA — five at left tackle, two at right guard and one at right tackle — before transferring to Stanford for the 2025 season. He missed Stanford's first three games of the 2026 season with an undisclosed injury before returning at left tackle.

Brandon is the author of the Trench Warfare newsletter , which focuses exclusively on offensive and defensive line evaluation. He also contributes as an analyst to Establish the Run , serves as the scouting coordinator for OL Masterminds and is a selection committee member for the Joe Moore Award .

Covers ground efficiently with good lateral quickness and enough range to expand with wide rushers, execute backside cutoffs and intersect targets away from his initial alignment.

Uses quick, forceful hands and generally good strike timing to establish first meaningful contact and disrupt rushers before they can fully access his frame.

Plays long when his hand placement is clean, using his length and grip to stay attached through the arc and widen rushers beyond the quarterback's drop.

Shows competitive strain and enough recovery ability to sustain after initial contact, with flashes of good torque and finish on combination blocks and cutoffs.

Needs more functional play strength to consistently brace, displace and overtake defenders. He can get pried open, jolted upright or worked underneath when his leverage is compromised.

Outside-hand placement too often lands down the middle of the rusher, shortening the corner and making speed-chop/rip combinations more effective than they should be.

Hip drift and body control create vulnerability to inside counters. Prongos can slide too far upfield, soften his inside shoulder or lunge when forced to redirect, putting him into recovery mode unnecessarily.

PLAYER ARCHETYPE : Athletic developmental LT with good range, twitch and hand quickness whose play strength and hand discipline need refinement to unlock starter-level consistency.

articles.title: Jaguars' Trevor Lawrence Talks MVP, Parker Washington, NFL Trade Deadline and More in B/R Interview
articles.summary: If Trevor Lawrence continues to play like he has this season, there could be an MVP award and Lombardi Trophy waiting for him.
articles.body:
If Trevor Lawrence continues to play like he has this season, there could be an MVP award and Lombardi Trophy waiting for him.

But at this point, he's happy his 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars are in the national consciousness.

"I remember a time when there weren't that many people talking about the Jags or about me, so we're just trying to keep that same chip on our shoulder and keep playing with that same fire," the quarterback told Bleacher Report.

Making the Case for NFL MVP Favorites And Darkhorses 🏆

Playing with a chip on his shoulder is working, as Lawrence has completed 66 percent of his passes for 2,284 yards, 21 touchdowns and just five interceptions. He also leads the league with 13.4 yards per completion, per Pro Football Reference , and is spreading the ball around with seven different Jaguars tallying double-digit receptions in the first nine games.

As a result, he is fourth in MVP odds on FanDuel Sportsbook behind only Joe Burrow, Josh Allen and Brock Purdy. He has also heard some of the noise, although he is more focused on making sure the wins continue to arrive in Jacksonville.

"To get the recognition is really cool," Lawrence said of the MVP race. "It's taken a lot of work to be in this position and to be even in consideration for it. Still, we're halfway through the season, so I even hesitate to say that because there's so much football left. That part of it is cool, but it's also not why I play.

"I'm always more focused on winning and the team aspect of the game. Nowadays, if your quarterback is playing well, the more you're going to win. So that stuff just happens if you're playing well and your team is a good team. I just want to keep playing well so we can keep winning. If the MVP comes with that, great. If not, that's fine too. We're just trying to win as many games as possible."

Winning is becoming routine under second-year head coach Liam Coen.

While the Jaguars were just 4-13 in 2024 the year before he arrived, they bounced back in a major way with a 13-4 record in his first season that ended with a loss in the Wild Card Round. The ceiling seems to be higher in his second season, as Lawrence looks even more comfortable in the offense with no shortage of weapons in the aerial attack in Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Brenton Strange.

Throw in two-way player Travis Hunter as an occasional option in the offense, Brian Thomas Jr. trying to find his footing with two touchdown catches and running back Bhayshul Tuten impressing, and the offensive-minded coach is getting the most out of all the firepower with continuity now in place.

"Consistency is a big part of it," Lawrence said. "So the longer you're with a coach or a system, the more comfortable you get. You've just seen these things a lot, and it helps you play faster. The chemistry with the guys on offense has also come a long way just being in year two in the system with familiarity with what we're doing and running.

"We're playing fast right now, the passing game is starting to get going and we've run the ball consistently all year. That combination of being able to run the ball and being able to throw the ball when we need to is huge. But we still have to keep finding ways to get better. We haven't fully arrived."

Perhaps nobody in that offensive attack outside of Lawrence himself has stood out more than Washington, who entered the league as a sixth-round draft pick in 2023 and wasn't a significant contributor in his first two seasons.

However, he had an immediate breakout season with Coen in 2025 with career-highs across the board with 58 catches for 847 yards and five touchdown catches and is on pace to break all those totals with ease this season with 36 catches for 645 yards and six scores in nine games.

It is more than just the numbers that stand out, as the Penn State product is making incredible contested catches, breaking free from defenders with his speed and fighting through double teams to become Lawrence's go-to option.

And the quarterback believes the best is yet to come.

"Parker is a special player," Lawrence said. "Everybody has gotten to see how well he's playing. It's no surprise to me, but I think about the plays I've missed with him. I missed one throw to him last game, and there were a couple other plays where he was open and had an opportunity to get the ball. So there's still so much left out there for us, and I think that's the exciting thing about it.

"That's how our team looks at things. We won the game, but we're not just happy with that. There are so many things that we need to get better at and we can improve. It's no different with Parker. He's playing great, but I know he can get even better and I can be better making sure he gets even more opportunities to make plays."

Having so many talented playmakers all over the field means the Jaguars consistently have candidates for the weekly FedEx Air & Ground NFL Awards, which recognize standout performances and also donates to Feeding America for a local partner food bank in the winning players' cities.

It is fitting, then, that Lawrence partnered with FedEx and Feeding America and its Jacksonville-based food bank partner, Feeding Northeast Florida, for the QB Kitchen campaign. He and TikTok chef Jack Macuso worked with Feeding America to create meal kits with the ingredients needed to recreate Lawrence's family-favorite sweet potato casserole recipe.

"It's been great working with FedEx," the Jaguars star said. "Obviously, they're a great company and the name speaks for itself with how long they've been around and been working with the NFL. The awards, you hear a lot about it and I've been fortunate enough to win it a couple of times, but it wasn't until last year I understood what it really meant.

"The donation that is triggered to Feeding Northeast Florida here in Jacksonville and to Feeding America to provide families with easier access and the ability to get food is huge. That part of it is really cool how they take something that is an individual performance to then help the community. I love what they're doing, and it's cool to be a part of it."

It was yet another way for him to give back to a community that has rallied around the Jaguars during such a thrilling start to the season.

And now there are even more notable players for the community to back, as Jacksonville was among the most aggressive teams at the NFL trade deadline. It landed safety Jessie Bates from the Atlanta Falcons, defensive tackle Jordan Davis from the Philadelphia Eagles and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints for a combined five draft picks.

While the front office paid quite the price, the aggression came as Jacksonville has a golden opportunity to reach the Super Bowl for the first time in franchise history. The moves also helped address a need with defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton expected to miss the remainder of the season with injury and added difference-makers to a defense that is already second in the league in points allowed per game.

Considering the Jaguars could have to face some combination of Allen, Patrick Mahomes and Burrow in the playoffs, improving what was already a strong defense made sense.

"We look at it as a positive as far as the belief in the team," Lawrence said. "We went out and got three really good players who are going to help our team. But I don't think you do that unless you already have a lot of belief in the team and you feel like we're good enough to go as far as we want to go. That showed the belief from the front office.

"Us as players, we still have the same job to do. Nobody is here to bail us out, we were playing really good football before and we have to keep that standard while adding the really good players to it. We still have to keep playing the way we've been playing and preparing the same way."

Playing that way has the Jaguars in full control of the AFC South at 7-2 and well ahead of the second-place Houston Texans, who are 3-6. Anything less than an easy division crown at this point would be a significant disappointment and a rather stunning development, but the team is eyeing more than an AFC South title.

The Buffalo Bills are 8-1, while the Kansas City Chiefs, Cincinnati Bengals and Denver Broncos are all 7-2. It is a loaded race for the top seed and the first-round bye that comes with it, and landing that spot would keep the Jaguars in Jacksonville through the Super Bowl.

Considering they have not lost in Jacksonville this season, it would be quite the boost.

"Anytime you have a realistic chance at that No. 1 seed, it can be really important," Lawrence said. "You try not to focus too much on that with so many games left. First things first, we have to take care of our division and make sure we keep winning all those games. When you're in the hunt for this potential No. 1 seed, it just makes every game that much more important.

"So I think it's good for our team to not lose focus at all, even for one week. It's good for us to have an extreme focus and attention to detail every week, especially since we play so many good teams down the stretch."

If Jacksonville follows Lawrence's example and makes it all the way to the Super Bowl, there will be even more people "talking about the Jags," which is exactly what he wants.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Indiana WR Nick Marsh

Nick Marsh is a physical, versatile wide receiver who can win in multiple ways in the passing game.

He brings strength and quickness in short areas as a boundary/X receiver. Marsh offers a big-slot target to create mismatches against smaller nickel corners.

He is in the middle of a career season after transferring from Michigan State to Indiana after two seasons. He set the Spartans' true freshman record for receiving yards and receptions in 2024.

Marsh is a former 4-star recruit in the 2024 class. He has an NFL-ready frame and game and is poised to become a dependable, impactful receiver at the next level.

Dame is the lead host of the Locked On NFL Draft podcast. Previously, he spent three years as a senior draft analyst for The Draft Network while evaluating draft prospects as the founder of The Scouting Room .

Compact and strong NFL-ready frame to thrive in high-traffic areas.

Nuanced route runner who attacks varying leverages and coverages effectively.

Short area quickness at the LOS to clear press-aligned CBs.

Spatial and sideline awareness to keep his feet in bounds; knowing where he is on the field needs improvement.

He's battled drops throughout his career.

Player Archetype : A strong, compact-built wide receiver with versatile alignment. He creates separation early in reps and has the strength to make physical catches. His play style resembles Chris Godwin, a power slot/movement receiver who will be a consistent playmaker at the next level.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Clemson Edge Will Heldt
articles.summary: Will Heldt's selling point is simple: a big dude with decent movement skills for his size. The 6'6", 260-pound edge defender can set the edge against tight ends and can push the pocket with a long arm while having a nice inside spin move as a counter.
articles.body:
Will Heldt's selling point is simple: a big dude with decent movement skills for his size. The 6'6", 260-pound edge defender can set the edge against tight ends and can push the pocket with a long arm while having a nice inside spin move as a counter.

However, he can struggle as a run defender against offensive tackles and isn't quite athletic or quick enough to be a stand-up outside linebacker, making it hard to find a natural scheme fit at the next level.

A 3-star recruit in the 2023 high school class, Heldt began his college career at Purdue. The Carmel, Ind. native was more of a special teamer as a true freshman before racking up 56 tackles, 10 for loss and five sacks to earn Honorable Mention All-Big Ten honors in year two for the Boilermakers.

Heldt transferred to Clemson ahead of the 2025 campaign and continued to rise, collecting 46 tackles, 15.5 TFLs and 7.5 sacks during his first year in Death Valley. That resulted in a Third-Team All-ACC bid.

Matt Holder has been a part of B/R's Scouting Department for five seasons. He also writes about the Las Vegas Raiders and NFL draft for SB Nation's Silver and Black Pride , and co-hosts a YouTube Channel, Tape Don't Lie , providing film breakdowns and more draft prospect analysis.

Heldt has the ideal build for an NFL edge defender, with good size and frame, and appears to have long arms.

Quick to get his hands up in both phases of the game.

Has some power as a pass-rusher to push the pocket with a long-arm move.

Nasty inside spin move that he uses as a counter to the spin, keeping offensive tackles guessing.

Won't get blocked by tight ends in the running game; he can win at the point of attack against them to set the edge and/or defeat blocks across their faces.

Heldt isn't very quick-twitched and isn't an elite athlete, making it difficult for him to work the edges as a pass-rusher.

Shows some lower-body stiffness, making it difficult to get clean wins or bend as a pass-rusher.

As a run defender, he gets minimal extension when taking on blocks from offensive tackles and struggles to disengage despite his length.

Doesn't have the sand in his pants/anchoring ability to take on combo blocks from tackles and tight ends when playing with his hand in the ground.

Lacks the speed and bend to make tackles near the line of scrimmage when unblocked on the backside of zone runs.

PLAY-STYLE ARCHETYPE : Versatile Edge defender (Aidan Hutchinson to Boogie Basham)

articles.title: Christian Kirk Injury Update, New NFL Rumors on Surgery After 49ers WR's Social Media Photo
articles.summary: After being placed on injured reserve for the second time this season earlier this month, San Francisco 49ers veteran wide receiver Christian Kirk won't be back on the field anytime soon.
articles.body:
After being placed on injured reserve for the second time this season earlier this month, San Francisco 49ers veteran wide receiver Christian Kirk won't be back on the field anytime soon.

Kirk posted a photo on Instagram revealing that he underwent meniscus surgery on his right knee. The post happened to be on his 30th birthday, and he wrote in the caption, "This year has been the hardest of my career."

After spending the previous three seasons with the Jacksonville Jaguars, Kirk signed a one-year deal with the 49ers this past offseason. Unfortunately, his move to the Bay Area got off to a rocky start when he suffered a calf strain in training camp, forcing him to start the year on IR.

After being activated last month, Kirk appeared in just one game, failing to catch his lone target of the season in San Francisco's Week 7 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. He didn't see the field again before being placed on IR for the second time on Nov. 7 due to his knee injury.

Kirk's absence hasn't hurt the 49ers too much, as they have the best record in the NFC at 8-1 and the No. 1 offense in the league with 399.8 total yards per game. Star quarterback Brock Purdy has been stellar, completing 70.1 percent of his passes for 2,369 yards, 20 touchdowns and five interceptions. Star tight end George Kittle leads the team with 44 catches for 557 yards and five touchdowns.

With Kirk still on the mend, the 49ers will try to keep things rolling when they return to action in a marquee matchup against the Minnesota Vikings (7-2) on Sunday Night Football .

He can circle-punch, snatch, and refit through contact, but average lateral quickness, late anchor timing, and vulnerability to redirection significantly limit his margin for error on the edge. His hand craft gives him functional pass-protection value, but the overall movement and play-strength profile projects more naturally to a rotational role than a developmental starter trajectory.

Azzopardi is a 6'7", 325-pound offensive line prospect who arrived at San Diego State as a 3-star recruit in the 2022 class. He redshirted after appearing in three games in 2022, then played in 12 games with six starts at right tackle in 2023 before transferring to Washington. Azzopardi started all 13 games at right tackle in 2024, made 11 starts there in 2025 while missing two games due to injury and has continued as Washington's starting right tackle in 2026.

Brandon is the author of the Trench Warfare newsletter , which focuses exclusively on offensive and defensive line evaluation. He also contributes as an analyst to Establish the Run , serves as the scouting coordinator for OL Masterminds and is a selection committee member for the Joe Moore Award .

Proactive, technically varied hands are the defining strength. He consistently looks to establish first meaningful contact and has shown effective circle-punch, independent-hand and snatch/trap answers against long arms and swipe attempts.

Good length and latch strength allow him to play at extension and remain attached even when his feet are not perfectly positioned. His hands can compensate for some athletic limitations and widen rushers who begin accessing the corner.

Can be sturdy once he is fit and settled, particularly when he times his strike correctly. His better reps show the ability to disrupt a rusher's path with hand timing and length rather than pure athletic range.

Functional positional run blocker who understands angles and to initially align his target with enough pop to impede their path.

Lateral quickness and high-side range are average. When speed gets to his upfield shoulder, his feet can lag and force him into recovery positions where he is relying heavily on hand strength rather than staying square.

Anchor timing is inconsistent. He can catch power with wide or high hands and concede too much ground before settling, particularly against speed-to-power.

Vulnerable to redirection at the top of the drop. Rushers who sell high side and work back inside can manipulate him out of position because his feet are slow to re-center and regain leverage.

Run-game play strength is functional rather than impactful. He is more of a placement blocker than a displacement blocker, and his feet can fall behind his latch when defenders work across his face.

PLAYER ARCHETYPE : Long, hand-savvy swing tackle with strong first meaningful contact and latch strength whose average range, anchor timing and play strength cap his starting ceiling.

articles.title: Browns QB Deshaun Watson Expresses Interest In Signing New Deal
articles.summary: Quarterback Deshaun Watson expressed an interest in playing for the Cleveland Browns beyond this season.
articles.body: Imagine reading that headline from the future two months ago. But, indeed, Deshaun Watson and the Cleveland Browns are 6-4 and in possession of the third AFC wild card seed, and the team's embattled starting quarterback is open to playing in Cleveland for the haul. "Yeah, of course," Watson said in a press conference on Wednesday afternoon when asked if he'd be open to signing a new deal with the Browns, according to 92.3 The Fan. "I want to continue to build on the legacy that I’m building, and again, ultimately, it’s up to the front office. It’s up to Jimmy and Dee [Haslam]; it’s up to [GM Andrew Berry]; it's up to Coach [Todd] Monken and the city. "So, at the end of the day, all I can do is continue to play good football, win games and let them kind of figure out what they want to do for the future." Watson is in the last season of a five-year, $230 million fully guaranteed deal, which he signed after being acquired by the Browns in 2022. With that said, the Browns restructured Watson's contract multiple times with roughly $86.2 million in prorated bonus charges remaining on his deal past this season. Through nine games this season (Watson missed Cleveland's Week 9 overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints due to a head injury), Watson has totaled 2,118 passing yards, seven passing touchdowns, four interceptions and an 89.1 passer rating, while completing 65.1% of his passes. He has also rushed for 266 yards and two scores. Last week, Watson and the Browns overcame a 17-point deficit at home to beat the Houston Texans, whom Cleveland acquired the three-time Pro Bowler from in 2022, to snap a two-game losing streak. Watson finished the comeback win with 312 passing yards, while rushing for 49 yards and one touchdown. "That’s up to my agent," Watson said of any potential contract talks with the Browns. "That’s all David Mulugheta [Watson's agent], so I don’t even worry about that. Even all the way up to the last game, my future and what that holds is all in God’s hands and whoever contacts David. "So, right now again, just playing good football, winning games, enjoying this moment because it can all be taken away regardless. Right now, I’m just focusing on today, this bye week and then getting back up here and finishing out the season strong." The Browns acquired Watson in a blockbuster trade with the Texans in 2022, which was preceded by him sitting out the 2021 season in the wake of requesting a trade and a double-digit number of sexual misconduct allegations emerging against him. Watson was suspended for 11 games in the 2022 season due to violating the NFL's personal-conduct policy and was limited to six starts – again – in 2023 due to a shoulder injury. Watson opened 2024 as Cleveland's starting quarterback, but he ruptured his Achilles seven games into the season and suffered a setback in the following months, keeping him off an NFL field until the 2026 season. In the preseason, Watson was booed by the Cleveland faithful, which he called "personal," citing how some of them cheered when he ruptured his Achilles in 2024. Watson went on to beat out second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders for the starting job. The nine games Watson has appeared in this season are the most in a single season for the 31-year-old since he started every game for the Texans in 2020.

However, ESPN president Jimmy Pitaro acknowledged the coverage it's generating is "disappointing":

Aikman is only adding fuel to the fire with his throwaway remark about Buck.

Monday Night Football has seven more games left on the schedule. The Houston Texans' trip to Lambeau Field to play the Green Bay Packers on Jan. 4 is set to be the last time Aikman and Buck call a came together.

articles.title: Justin Herbert and Madison Beer’s home draws police response after reported break-in takes new turn

articles.body: Police officers arrived at the Hollywood Hills home of singer Madison Beer and her fiancé, Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert, on Wednesday night, November 18, after receiving a report of a possible break-in. The call led to a large police response, with video showing the couple outside their property as officers arrived. However, after checking the house, the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) said no crime had occurred.Madison Beer and Justin Herbert’s home draws LAPD response after reported break-inAccording to ABC7 Los Angeles, officers from the LAPD’s Hollywood Division received a call about a possible break-in shortly before 8 p.m. on Wednesday. The situation was initially reported as a break-in, but dispatchers upgraded the call to a burglary after speaking with the person who contacted the police.The report also stated that two male suspects had allegedly entered the property, which is listed under Madison Beer’s name in property records. This led to a larger police response in the Hollywood Hills neighborhood.When officers reached the house, they searched the building but did not find the suspects. More importantly, their investigation did not uncover any evidence of a crime. LAPD confirmed to ABC7 that officers at the scene determined that no crime had taken place.Video from outside the property appeared to show Madison Beer and Justin Herbert standing together and speaking with police officers. The footage also showed several police vehicles near the residence as officers looked into the report.Although the call raised concerns about the couple’s safety, there has been no confirmation of an actual break-in or any injuries. Police have also not shared further details about what led to the original report.Madison Beer and Justin Herbert’s engagement and Chargers seasonThe police response comes as Madison Beer and Justin Herbert continue to attract attention for their relationship. The singer and NFL quarterback were first linked in July 2025, and their relationship became public later that year when they were spotted kissing on the sidelines before a Los Angeles Chargers game against the Washington Commanders in October.In July 2026, the couple announced their engagement on social media. Beer shared pictures of Herbert’s proposal in a garden and introduced him as her fiancé with a short caption. Since then, she has also been seen supporting him during the Chargers’ difficult NFL season.Even her recent appearance at ELLE’s 2026 Women in Hollywood event did not stop her from following the Chargers’ game. Her stylist and creative director, Harper Slate, shared a picture on Instagram Stories showing Beer watching the game on her phone while attending the event.Slate wrote, “When we have a carpet but football is on,” showing how the singer was keeping up with Herbert despite being at a red-carpet event.Meanwhile, the Chargers finally secured a win on Monday, November 16, defeating the Baltimore Ravens 23-20. It was their first victory of the 2026 season after an 11-game losing streak dating back to the previous season.Herbert completed 12 of 18 passes for 129 yards and also ran for 51 yards and a touchdown. Running back Omarion Hampton played a major part in the win, recording 105 rushing yards and a touchdown.According to the Los Angeles Times, the victory moved the Chargers to a 1-8 record.
