articles.title: Riley Moss, Broncos Reportedly Agree to Contract Extension, Details Revealed in New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos and cornerback Riley Moss reportedly agreed to a contract extension Thursday.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos and cornerback Riley Moss reportedly agreed to a contract extension Thursday.

Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network first reported the deal. According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , Moss' contract is worth $67 million over four years.

Moss, 26, is in the midst of his fourth NFL season after Denver selected him in the third round of the 2023 NFL draft out of Iowa.

Insider's Take on Pats, Maye Contract Talks

While 2024 NFL Defensive Player of the Year Patrick Surtain II rightfully receives much of the credit for Denver's success on defense, Moss has been a key figure in his own right as the starter opposite Surtain for the past three seasons.

Moss started all 14 games he appeared in during the 2024 season, recording 86 tackles, eight passes defended and one interception. He followed that up last season by starting 17 games and finishing with 80 tackles, one pick and a league-high 19 passes defensed.

Through eight games this season, Moss has registered 27 tackles, three pass breakups and one interception for a Broncos team that is tied with the Kansas City Chiefs for the AFC West lead at 7-2.

The Broncos are attempting to reach the playoffs for a third consecutive season, and defense has been the driving force behind the team's overall success during that stretch.

Denver ranked seventh in total defense and third in scoring defense in 2024, and second in total defense and third in scoring defense last season when it made it all the way to the AFC Championship Game.

The Broncos once again boast a top-10 scoring defense this season, as they rank ninth in the category, but they are surprisingly just 27th in total defense.

That includes ranking 20th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game, although opposing quarterbacks have the eighth-worst quarterback rating in the league against Denver's defense at just 83.3.

By and large, defense has been the Broncos' strength, and all signs point toward that continuing to be the case this season and in the future.

With Moss sporting a new, four-year extension and Surtain signed through 2029, the Broncos' secondary is set for years to come, locking in one of the team's greatest assets.

articles.title: Week 11 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em, Play or Bench Advice on Top Fantasy Football NFL Stars
articles.summary: Week 11 will get underway on Thursday night when the Indianapolis Colts visit the Houston Texans.
articles.body:
Week 11 will get underway on Thursday night when the Indianapolis Colts visit the Houston Texans.

While the Colts have essentially punted on their 2026 season by trading several key players, the Texans are still scrapping to stay in the playoff hunt. At this point in the season, many football managers can relate.

Injuries and unexpected surprises—like Houston's defense becoming a major liability—have left some managers on the brink of elimination and without several stars.

The Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams, New England Patriots, and Seattle Seahawks are also on bye this week.

Let's examine some of the best and worst matchups for second-tier stars based on recent production, projected roles, and point-per-reception scoring.

He couldn't do enough to deliver a win in Week 10, but Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott did just about all he could. He gashed the San Francisco 49ers for 343 yards, five touchdowns, and 35.4 fantasy points.

This week, Prescott will have to keep pace with a Tennessee Titans offense that is starting to find a rhythm. He may not have to carry the Cowboys the way he did against San Francisco, but he should have another big outing.

Tennessee has surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing QBs this season. Other Week 11 starts:

Jared Goff tends to be a dependable starter, regardless of matchup, but managers who have other QB options should explore them. The Detroit Lions are set to host a very good Tampa Bay Buccaneers defense that has had two weeks to prepare.

Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams still put up a respectable 16.8 fantasy points when he played Tampa two weeks ago, but he also threw four interceptions. The Bucs have surrendered the fourth-fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks this season.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Start: Emmett Johnson, Kansas City Chiefs

Kansas City Chiefs rookie Emmett Johnson was working his way into flex territory even before starting running back Kenneth Walker III suffered a groin injury. With Walker out of the lineup, Johnson went off against the Atlanta Falcons for 35.1 fantasy points last week.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Chiefs may let Walker rest for another week. Even if Walker returns, Johnson should see a sizeable role against the Arizona Cardinals.

The Cardinals have surrendered an average of 20.5 fantasy points to opposing RBs. Other Week 11 starts:

It'll be hard to sit Cam Skattebo during a six-team bye week. However, the New York Giants starter is poised to disappoint against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Jacksonville has surrendered the fourth-fewest fantasy points to opposing running backs this season, and they're set to debut new defensive tackle Jordan Davis in Week 11.

New Orleans Saints rookie Jordyn Tyson just made his NFL debut in Week 9, but he has already established himself as a go-to target for Tyler Shough.

Tyson had 11 catches on 13 targets last week and finished with 19 fantasy points. He could have a similar outing against an inconsistent Chicago Bears secondary that is heavily focused on slowing Chris Olave.

Rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza had a respectable debut against the Seattle Seahawks last week. However, he clearly lacked the chemistry with top perimeter receiver Tre Tucker that former starter Kirk Cousins had.

Tucker caught one of only two targets for nine yards and finished with his second-lowest fantasy total of the season. This week, he'll face a Denver Broncos defense that has surrendered the sixth-fewest fantasy points to opposing WRs.

The Buffalo Bills eventually pulled away from the New York Jets in Week 10, but it was a slog for most of the game. Buffalo could face a similar situation against the Miami Dolphins in Week 11.

Expect Josh Allen to rely on tight end Dalton Kincaid to help put away the Dolphins. Miami has been fairly solid against opposing receivers but has surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends.

Kincaid should hit double digits after delivering just 7.8 fantasy points last week. Other Week 11 starts:

Chigoziem Okonkwo, Washington Commanders

Dolphins tight end Greg Dulcich was starting to establish some sleeper value with Malik Willis in the lineup. With Willis on injured reserve and Kyle McCord behind center, managers should dump Dulcich.

Dulcich was targeted only twice against the Colts last week and finished without a catch. He's unlikely to fare much better against the Bills, who have surrendered an average of 9.7 fantasy points to opposing tight ends.

articles.title: Bill Belichick, Robert Kraft Advance to Final Stage of 2027 Pro Football HOF Class Selection Process
articles.summary: Longtime New England Patriots head coach Bill Belichick and owner Robert Kraft both advanced to the final stage of the selection process for the Pro Football Hall of Fame's class of 2027 this week.
articles.body:
Longtime New England Patriots head coach Bill Belichick and owner Robert Kraft both advanced to the final stage of the selection process for the Pro Football Hall of Fame's class of 2027 this week.

The Pro Football Hall of Fame announced Thursday that Belichick advanced through the coach subcommittee, beating out Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan, while Kraft was voted into the next round by the contributor subcommittee over Ralph Hay, Virginia McCaskey, Doug Williams and John Wooten.

Now, Belichick and Kraft are set to join a group of 13 yet-to-be-determined players, and the selection committee will vote on which of those 15 candidates earn enshrinement into the Pro Football Hall of Fame for 2027.

NFL Head Coaching Changes That Must Be Made 🏈

Belichick and Kraft won six Super Bowls together with the Patriots, making both of them strong contenders to secure induction into the Hall of Fame.

The 74-year-old Belichick was head coach of the Pats from 2000 to 2023 following a lengthy run as an NFL assistant and stint as head coach of the Cleveland Browns.

Belichick won two Super Bowls as the New York Giants' defensive coordinator, and then six more as head coach of the Patriots with quarterback Tom Brady helping him to lead the way.

A three-time NFL Coach of the Year, Belichick ranks third in NFL history in regular-season coaching wins with 302, first in playoff coaching wins with 31 and second in combined coaching wins with 333.

Belichick parted ways with the Patriots at the end of the 2023 season, and he is in the midst of his second season as head football coach at the University of North Carolina.

The 85-year-old Kraft purchased the Patriots in 1994, and he achieved almost instant success, as they reached the Super Bowl in the 1996 season.

However, it wasn't until Kraft hired Belichick and oversaw the draft selection of Brady in 2000 that the Patriots became the closest thing to an NFL dynasty in the 2000s and 2010s.

Even after Belichick and Brady left the organization, Kraft managed to reach his 11th career Super Bowl last season, although New England fell to the Seattle Seahawks in the big game.

The Pro Football Hall of Fame selection committee will submit its votes for the class of 2027 prior to Super Bowl LXI, which will take place on Feb. 14, 2027.

A coach, contributor or player requires 80 percent of the vote from the selection committee to be named a Hall of Famer, and between three and seven Hall of Famers can be chosen each year.

As has been the case for the past several years, the Pro Football Hall of Fame's class of 2027 will likely be announced during the NFL Honors awards show, just days before the Super Bowl.

articles.title: Troy Aikman makes dig at Joe Buck on Dallas radio show amid ongoing tensions: 'I know Joe's always wanted a one-man booth'
articles.summary: The strained relationship between the 'Monday Night Football' broadcasting duo has been growing over the past few months.
articles.body:
Troy Aikman and Joe Buck might be staying professional on "Monday Night Football" broadcasts, but the off-field rift seems to only be growing wider. Amid ongoing tensions between the ESPN broadcasting pair, Aikman took a jab at Buck on Thursday while on a Dallas radio show.

Aikman made the dig while appearing on "The Musers" on Dallas' 96.7 The Ticket, a radio show the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback regularly joins. With co-hosts Craig Miller and Gordon Keith both out for the show, George Dunham was hosting by himself. Aikman noted that Dunham was "flying solo," prompting Dunham to make a joke about Aikman joining him as a host.

That led Aikman to make a surprising swipe at Buck: "I know Joe's always wanted a one-man booth, I'm wondering if you've always wanted a one-man radio show," Aikman said, via Awful Announcing .

Dunham laughed off the comment and joked that he and Buck had a lot in common, before mentioning that Buck had been a presenter at the Country Music Awards on Wednesday, joking that "he's everywhere."

"Everywhere. Ubiquitous," Aikman agreed, though the tone of that agreement was not clear.

Tensions between the pair have appeared to be growing in the past few weeks, boiling over with a well-publicized fight in the "MNF" booth last month. The issues reportedly stem from Buck signing an offseason extension with ESPN worth over $100 million, while Aikman has not been offered a new deal.

Following news of the fight, Aikman confirmed to 96.7 The Ticket on Oct. 15 that he would be a free agent after this season and said he's looking forward to "where my next landing spot might be."

Aikman and Buck, who began broadcasting as a pair in 2002 at Fox, are the longest-tenured broadcast duo in the league. The two moved from Fox to ESPN together in 2022.

As the rift is seemingly set to break that partnership up, there might be some other moving pieces as Aikman finds his next position. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones told reporters last month that he has already offered Aikman, who spent his entire NFL career with Dallas, a job with the team after his contract ends. Former New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees, meanwhile, has expressed interest in replacing Aikman in the booth.

articles.title: Marlon Humphrey sent home from Ravens facility, will be inactive Week 11 after joking that Baltimore is 'best at making criminals'
articles.summary: Humphrey joked that Baltimore is "best at making criminals" on an episode of his podcast earlier this week.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens have sent cornerback Marlon Humphrey home from the team facility on Thursday as part of the fallout from a joke about the city of Baltimore earlier this week.

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed with reporters that Humphrey will be inactive for Week 11's contest against the Carolina Panthers as a result of those comments. Minter cited "internal conversations" in the decision, and confirmed that Humphrey would be out for only this week, at least for now.

"Truthfully, I know there's gonna be a lot of questions. Most of it, again I said this yesterday, these conversations are very, very personal and private and, to me, they need to remain that for the good of the team and the organization," Minter said, via ESPN's Jamison Hensley .

Humphrey initially made the comment on an episode of "The Marlon Humphrey Show" that was released Wednesday. When asked what Baltimore was best at making, Humphrey mentioned "The Star Spangled Banner" and National Bohemian beer before making a derogatory comment that has received widespread criticism.

"What is Baltimore best at making?" Humphrey pondered . "They're best at making criminals."

Humphrey, who has spent his entire 10-year career in Baltimore, acknowledged the comments with an apology at his locker Wednesday.

"I would like to apologize for some comments on my podcast I had yesterday to the city of Baltimore," Humphrey said, via The Baltimore Banner's Kyle Goon . "As you guys know, I've been here my whole career. Spent lots of offseasons here. Welcomed a son here, and I'm an investor in the city. … And, obviously, I do know the effect that words have and just would like to apologize for those comments."

On Thursday, Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver chimed in on the issue, saying the team was focused on winning on Sunday but that he still had faith in Humphrey and the members of the team.

"We love him," Weaver said of Humphrey, via Hensley . "As a dad, as a coach, as a Christian, it's important to say that I can love the man, have respect for him, and disagree with what he said in this particular moment."

Following the apology, Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott posted about the incident on social media , saying in a statement that Humphrey's "verbal apology is not enough."

"Baltimore is a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives and to have someone that looks like them who wears a Baltimore Ravens jersey relegate them to becoming criminals cuts deeper," Scott said.

Scott also invited Humphrey to sit down with him and talk with a group of Baltimoreans "who have re-entered into our community and are now preventing others from making the mistakes they made." It is unclear if Humphrey has accepted Scott's offer.

articles.body:
Ahmad Moten is a gap-shooting defensive tackle who can get penetration with his impressive get-off, quickness and overall athleticism. He's also a disruptive interior pass-rusher who made a name for himself during Miami's 2025 National Championship run. However, the 6'3", 300-pound defensive lineman's draft stock has taken a hit with a disappointing 2026 campaign.

A 3-star recruit in the 2022 high school class, Moten wasn't a significant part of the Hurricanes' defensive line rotation until his redshirt sophomore season. He recorded 18 tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss and a sack in 13 games that year, before enjoying a breakout performance in 2025 with 31 tackles, nine TFLs and 4.5 sacks in 14 contests. The latter resulted in a second-team All-ACC bid.

Matt Holder has been a part of B/R's Scouting Department for five seasons. He also writes about the Las Vegas Raiders and NFL draft for SB Nation's Silver and Black Pride , and co-hosts a YouTube Channel, Tape Don't Lie , providing film breakdowns and more draft prospect analysis.

Moton is quick off the ball and accelerates off the line of scrimmage well to shoot gaps and get penetration off the snap.

Has the agility and lateral movement skills to get into the backfield when slanting, too.

As a pass-rusher, he has decent hand usage to work the offensive lineman's hands after contact.

Good hand swipe and swim moves that he can win with as a pass-rusher.

Has the quickness and agility to work the edges and beat offensive linemen across their faces.

Agility also helps him be an effective looper on line games.

Moton plays with inconsistent pad level off the line of scrimmage, hurting the effectiveness of his bull rush and making it difficult to take on combo blocks.

Appears to have shorter arms, limiting his extension on blocks and making it difficult to escape/shed. Also leads to offensive linemen making the first significant contact when he's rushing the passer.

Struggles to sink his hips and anchor as a run defender, leading to him getting washed up the field or inside and into the trash.

Lack of an anchor can also lead to him getting pancaked by double teams or combo blocks.

PLAY-STYLE ARCHETYPE : One-gap defensive tackle (Ed Oliver to Quinton Jefferson)

Kelley Jones is a shutdown corner in the low red zone whose imposing body and long arms create mismatches at every turn. His high school experience as a safety has helped him become an incredibly sound zone player with unteachable tools at cornerback. Collegiate quarterbacks don't want to test the rangy defender, so he's busy keeping a blanket on his side of the field.

The former 3- star recruit anchors a Mississippi State team looking to surprise people this season, and they are off to a good start. Excellent zone instincts on the perimeter and uses his eyes to tie routes to the quarterback and take them away.

The 6'3", 196-pound corner is an imposing body type with the length and ball skills to disrupt the catch point.

He brings versatility and range that allow him to play multiple places on the back end and cover ground.

His backpedal pad level in man coverage has improved, allowing him to change direction more quickly and stay in the hip pocket.

Hand usage and ball tracking down the sideline give Jones an advantage in one-on-one situations.

In man coverage, Jones is more tools than technique and will open the gate too quickly to receivers.

He lacks refined press strike timing and struggles to mirror in space, putting him in difficult positions.

Jones has great size and length, but must clean up his tackling technique to clean up plays and limit yards after the catch or contact.

There are hitches in his transitions that limit quick changes of direction, and decelerating can be difficult when his pad level gets high.

articles.title: Cowboys' Christian Parker Reacts to Losing Play-Calling Duties, 'Not an Ideal Situation for Me'
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys made the decision to strip defensive coordinator Christian Parker of his play-calling duties this week amid the team's floundering play on that side of the ball, turning the responsibility over to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys made the decision to strip defensive coordinator Christian Parker of his play-calling duties this week amid the team's floundering play on that side of the ball, turning the responsibility over to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine.

Parker, understandably, told reporters on Thursday that he wasn't thrilled with the decision but understood why it was made and begrudgingly accepted it:

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer maintained that Parker remains a "critical piece of what we're trying to do as we search for answers and solutions" while speaking to reporters on Wednesday.

"I think he has an incredibly bright future not just this year but beyond with us," he continued. "He's still the defensive coordinator of our football team. He's still running meetings. He's still leading walkthroughs. The only thing that's different is he's not calling the plays on gameday."

Still, losing play-calling duties is undeniably a demotion of sorts.

It's possible that Parker, 34, has been made something of a scapegoat for the team's defensive woes this season. While the Cowboys made a number of changes to the defensive core in the past year, the personnel on that side of the ball is still clearly lacking.

Regardless, something had to change in Dallas.

The Cowboys rank dead last in yards allowed (393.8 YPG) and are 30th in both points surrendered (28.2 PPG) and takeaways (eight). Those woes came to a head on Sunday, when the team gave up 584 yards of total offense and three touchdowns of 65 or more yards in a 46-40 loss against the San Francisco 49ers.

If the Cowboys continue to struggle on defense against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, Parker might find himself off the hook for some of this season's struggles. But for now, the first-year defensive coordinator has been forced to accept a diminished role.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for LSU Edge Princewill Umanmielen
articles.summary: Princewill Umanmielen is an explosive athlete who can win with speed around the edge and is twitchy enough to beat offensive tackles across their faces as a pass rusher. However, the 6'4", 256-pound edge defender doesn't make much of an impact against the run and profiles as a "designated pass rusher" in the NFL.
articles.body:
Princewill Umanmielen is an explosive athlete who can win with speed around the edge and is twitchy enough to beat offensive tackles across their faces as a pass rusher. However, the 6'4", 256-pound edge defender doesn't make much of an impact against the run and profiles as a "designated pass rusher" in the NFL.

A 4-star recruit in the 2023 high school class, Umanmielen began his college career at Nebraska, where he was a second-team freshman All-American. He played in 23 games (one start) for the Cornhuskers, collecting 35 tackles, seven tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks before transferring to Ole Miss in 2025.

The former Rebel enjoyed a breakout campaign in his lone season at Oxford, posting 44 tackles, 13.0 TFLs, nine sacks, and an interception to earn third-team All-SEC honors. Then, Umanmielen followed head coach Lane Kiffin to LSU in the offseason.

Princewill's brother, Princely, was a third-round pick in the 2025 draft class by the Carolina Panthers.

Matt Holder has been a part of B/R's Scouting Department for five seasons. He also writes about the Las Vegas Raiders and NFL draft for SB Nation's Silver and Black Pride , and co-hosts a YouTube Channel, Tape Don't Lie , providing film breakdowns and more draft prospect analysis.

Umanmielen has good size and appears to have good arm length for an NFL edge defender, on top of being a very good and twitchy athlete.

Explosive off the line of scrimmage to threaten offensive tackles with speed as a pass-rusher.

Sets up his pass rush moves well by stemming inside or outside to win in the opposite direction or by using a hesitation move.

Impressive quickness and change of direction skills to beat tackles across their faces.

Decent at turning speed to power, he can get an initial push to put tackles on their heels and escape for a sack if the quarterback steps up in the pocket.

Flexible lower body, showing good bend to corner at the top of the rush. Also has the speed and bend to make tackles when unblocked on the backside of zone runs.

Speed and agility make him an effective looper on line games.

Comfortable dropping into coverage occassionally. He can spot drop and rally to make tackles after the catch.

Despite adding weight at LSU (listed at 245 pounds on Ole Miss' 2025 roster ), Umanmielen still lacks the sand in his pants to set the edge against NFL-caliber offensive tackles.

Subpar upper body strength limits his extension on blocks, making it hard for him to escape.

Doesn't have the rotational strength to avoid getting his shoulders turned when taking on combo/scoop blocks.

Isn't good at recognizing reach blocks and running his feet to avoid getting pinned inside against outside runs.

Can be a little late to use his hands as a pass-rusher.

PLAY-STYLE ARCHETYPE : Designated Edge Rusher (Joseph Ossai to Darrell Taylor)

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Texas Tech DL A.J. Holmes Jr.
articles.summary: A.J. Holmes has been a major riser in the 2026 College Football season, showcasing a well-rounded skill set.
articles.body:
A.J. Holmes has been a major riser in the 2026 College Football season, showcasing a well-rounded skill set.

The 6'3", 300-pound defensive tackle has the strength to defeat one-on-one blocks against the run and the athleticism and quickness to be an effective interior pass rusher. However, he lacks NFL-level length and struggles to anchor against double teams.

A 3-star recruit in the 2022 high school class, Holmes' college career began at Houston. He spent three seasons with the Cougars, collecting 67 tackles, 13.5 tackles for loss and 4.5 sacks in 29 games (16 starts).

The Houston native transferred to Texas Tech ahead of the 2025 campaign and began the season as a backup to Skyler Gill-Howard (Lions' 2026 sixth-round pick) until Gill-Howard's injury.

Holmes ended up playing in all 14 games (nine starts) and racking up 38 tackles, 9.0 TFLs, 4.5 sacks and four passes defended to earn second-team All-American and first-team All-Big 12 recognition.

Matt Holder has been a part of B/R's Scouting Department for five seasons. He also writes about the Las Vegas Raiders and NFL draft for SB Nation's Silver and Black Pride , and co-hosts a YouTube Channel, Tape Don't Lie , providing film breakdowns and more draft prospect analysis.

Holmes has impressive upper body strength to win at the point of attack against base blocks, standing up interior offensive linemen and/or resetting the line of scrimmage.

Quick to get his hands up against the run and has plenty of strength to stack and shed, allowing him to make tackles in his gap.

Shifts his eyes and hands to take on down blocks and avoid getting washed inside.

Has decent quickness to beat interior offensive linemen across their faces, either as a run defender or pass-rusher.

Solid get-off and keeps his feet moving through contact to be an effective bull rusher.

Has flashed several pass-rush moves that he can win with: spin, push-pull, swim and hand swipe.

Active hands as a pass-rusher and works the hands after contact.

Good motor as a pass-rusher to get coverage or clean up sacks

Offers some scheme/alignment versatility with the ability to play as a 3- or 4i-technique in even or odd fronts.

Holmes lacks the ideal length for an NFL defensive tackle, appearing to have shorter arms, which limits how much extension he can get on blocks and allows long-limbed offensive linemen to make the first significant contact when rushing the passer.

Waist bender instead of a knee bender to get low.

Pad level issues and lack of anchoring ability cause him to get pushed out of his gap frequently when taking on combo blocks/double teams.

Late to see/react to reach or combo blocks and lacks the lateral movement skills to avoid getting wheeled out of his gap.

A little tight-hipped, making it difficult to get clean wins around the edges when working finesse moves.

Could afford to rush with more of a plan and work countermoves when his initial move doesn't work.

PLAY-STYLE ARCHETYPE : Versatile Interior Defensive Lineman (John Franklin-Myers to Brandon Dorlus)

articles.title: Mike Florio and Chris Simms apologize after NFL calls their Mike Vrabel mustache joke ‘offensive’
articles.summary: The NFL has called out NBC Sports host Mike Florio and his co-host Chris Simms for making an offensive joke about New England Patriots head coach Mike
articles.body: The NFL has called out NBC Sports host Mike Florio and his co-host Chris Simms for making an offensive joke about New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel’s mustache. The comments came during a discussion about the Patriots’ recent trip to Germany and their 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich. NFL executive Jeff Miller described the remarks as inappropriate and offensive. Florio and Simms have since issued a joint apology through NBC Sports, following criticism of their comments about Vrabel’s facial hair.Mike Florio's Hitler Reference About Mike Vrabel's Mustache Draws NFL CriticismThe controversy started during the November 17 episode of Pro Football Talk Live. Florio and Simms were discussing the Patriots' loss to the Lions when the conversation turned to Vrabel's new mustache.Simms called it a "German mustache" and joked that the coach was following the German theme during his visit to Munich. Florio then added a comment about being careful while trimming the sides of the mustache in Germany.Although neither host mentioned Adolf Hitler by name, their comments were widely understood as a reference to the former German dictator, whose small toothbrush-style mustache became one of his most recognizable features.The exchange continued even after the show's producer, Gary Carter, appeared to disapprove of the joke. Florio noticed his reaction and responded, "It's funny, Gary. It was 80 years ago. Let us have some fun, for crying out loud."The remarks quickly became a bigger issue than the discussion about the Patriots' performance. Many people found the comparison distasteful, especially because of the history behind the reference.The NFL also made its position clear. Jeff Miller, the league's executive vice president of communications, public affairs and policy, told Front Office Sports that the comments had crossed a line."We found the remarks inappropriate and offensive," Miller said in his statement.According to Front Office Sports, the NFL also contacted NBC Sports about the incident. The network is the broadcaster behind Pro Football Talk Live, where Florio and Simms made the comments.Mike Florio and Chris Simms Issue Joint Apology After NFL's ResponseThe criticism eventually led to a response from both hosts. On Wednesday, November 18, Florio and Simms released a joint apology through NBC Sports."On yesterday's PFT Live show, we made comments that some found offensive and we apologize," they wrote.The statement did not explain the comments further or name the people who had raised concerns. However, it came only hours after the NFL publicly criticized their remarks.Florio has been covering professional football for more than two decades. He started ProFootballTalk in 2001 and later partnered with NBC Sports. He also appears on the network's Football Night in America coverage.Simms, a former NFL quarterback, has worked with NBC Sports since 2016. Both men were part of the discussion that led to the league's response.Meanwhile, Vrabel has other problems to deal with as the Patriots look to recover from their difficult trip to Germany.New England fell to 5-5 after losing to Detroit. The defeat was also the team's second straight loss following its 45-27 defeat against the Green Bay Packers on November 8.Quarterback Drake Maye's injury added to the team's concerns. He left the Munich game with an ankle injury after being sacked by Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson in the first quarter. Maye did not return, and backup quarterback Tommy DeVito took over.Vrabel said after the game that Maye would need further tests to find out how serious the injury was. The Patriots also have a Week 11 bye, giving the quarterback extra time to recover before their next game.New England is scheduled to face the Los Angeles Chargers on November 29. articles.title: Troy Aikman escalates ongoing feud with Joe Buck, saying broadcast partner ‘always wanted a one-man booth’
articles.summary: This NFL season was supposed to be a celebration for ESPN, as it prepares to host its first Super Bowl.
articles.body: This NFL season was supposed to be a celebration for ESPN, as it prepares to host its first Super Bowl. Instead, the spotlight remains on the network’s top football broadcast booth over the tension between longtime partners Joe Buck and analyst Troy Aikman. While Buck re-signed with ESPN on a long-term, lucrative contract in September, Aikman has been working without an extension to a deal that is set to expire in 2027. The potential breakup of the broadcast team that has worked together for a quarter-century sparked a reported argument in October, and on Thursday Aikman turned up speculation while calling out Buck during his weekly appearance on a Dallas sports radio station. “I know Joe’s always wanted a one-man booth,” Aikman told 96.7 The Ticket. Aikman and Buck had spent two decades working together calling games for Fox before they each arrived at ESPN in 2022 as part of an overhaul of the network’s flagship “Monday Night Football” broadcast. Both arrived on five-year contracts. As this season began, Buck told Front Office Sports in September that “Troy Aikman knows that I have his back. … He knows I’m his biggest fan, vice versa.” Days later, numerous outlets reported Buck had re-signed with the network on a six-year contract worth more than $100 million. Aikman’s deal was set to expire after the Super Bowl. Signs of discord over Buck’s job security at ESPN, and Aikman’s lack of a guaranteed future there, first became public when outlets reported the two had argued before calling an Oct. 12 game between the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams. The Athletic later reported that prior to Buck and Aikman’s argument, Aikman had met with ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro about his future and his relationship with Buck. “There’s probably a time and a place for all that,” Aikman said of dynamic with Buck on Oct. 15. “I don’t know if now is the time. I don’t know if it’s hard to figure out kind of what happened. I’ll broadcast through this season and I’ll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens. I’m looking forward to whatever the rest of this season does hold and the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot may be.” Pitaro called the timing of media coverage of Buck and Aikman’s falling out “disappointing,” as February’s Super Bowl will be ESPN’s first. “They’ve done a great job for ESPN, they’ve done a great job for the league, they’ve done a great job for the game, and most importantly, they’ve done a great job for fans. Are we happy about the media coverage recently? Of course not. It’s been disappointing,” Pitaro said this week. “But these guys are professionals, and they’re delivering every week. If you watched it last night, another super high-quality production and telecast, and I’d fully expect that to continue that through the season and through the Super Bowl.”

articles.title: Ravens didn't discipline receiver over a domestic arrest but deactivate Marlon Humphrey over podcast comments
articles.summary: Marlon Humphrey apologized for saying Baltimore is best at making criminals, but the Ravens still deactivated him for Sunday at the Carolina Panthers.
articles.body: The Baltimore Ravens sent cornerback Marlon Humphrey home, and he will not practice and will be deactivated for Sunday's game at the Carolina Panthers, coach Jesse Minter announced Thursday. The reason for all this is apparently because Humphrey hurt some people's feelings. "After a lot of internal conversations between obviously with myself and leadership of the organization, we decided to deactivate Marlon for this game this upcoming week," Minter told reporters at his regularly scheduled media availability. "And so, truthfully, I know there's going to be a lot of questions. Most of it, again, I said this yesterday, like these conversations are very, very personal and private, and to me, need to remain that for the good of the team and the organization." Minter said the deactivation will be one game — "for now." WHAT IS BALTIMORE BEST AT MAKING? 'CRIMINALS,' SAYS MARLON HUMPHREY WHO THEN FEELS THE HEAT AND CHANGES TUNE RAVENS PLAYERS RIDE WITH PRESIDENT TRUMP IN MOTORCADE, GET SHOUTOUT DURING SPEECH AT BALTIMORE SHIPYARD EVENT And it is not known if this deactivation had anything to do with an internal disagreement of any kind between Humphrey and club leadership beyond his words on his podcast this week. But if there was no such internal club episode, what we have is the Baltimore Ravens suspending a good player who has started 123 games since joining the team in 2017 because he took liberties on his podcast this week in responding to the question, "What is Baltimore best at making?" "They're best at making criminals," Humphrey said half-jokingly. And, yes, that set off a lot of people in Baltimore. Some of those people are apparently within and outside the Ravens organization. But Wednesday, Humphrey apologized for his off-the-cuff remark. JOSH JACOBS 'REMORSEFUL' IN FIRST COMMENTS SINCE DOMESTIC ABUSE ARREST LED TO COMMISSIONER'S EXEMPT LIST STAY "I do know the effect that words have," Humphrey told reporters surrounding his locker stall. "I'd just like to apologize for those comments." Not enough, apparently. Baltimore mayor Brandon Scott went on his Instagram account and made Humphrey's comment about race. Humphrey, by the way, is Black. The Ravens, obviously feeling community pressure, decided Humphrey's apology fell short of their pound-of-flesh disciplinary requirements. "I would say this, you know, he's very remorseful," Minter said. "I think he really understands, you know, that words mean a lot, especially to the people in the city. And, you know, when you say something like that, it's not a reflection of our team and our organization and how we want to operate." This is utterly ridiculous, folks. NFL RESTARTS SOCIAL JUSTICE MESSAGING WHILE BATTLING DOMESTIC ABUSE, DRUNK DRIVING AND PROSTITUTION ARRESTS The Baltimore Ravens, struggling to rally after losing five consecutive games and watching their playoff hopes fade with every passing week, are sitting one of the better players because he said something dumb. And this is where we understand precisely how preposterous this disciplinary action is: Compare it to how the Ravens handled receiver Rashod Bateman’s charges tied to a domestic violence incident in June. Bateman was arrested on charges of first-degree criminal damage to property (felony property damage), battery (family violence), and reckless conduct after he allegedly used an object to smash the windshield and driver's side window of a Mercedes-Benz belonging to the mother of his child. The woman and the couple's three-month-old child were inside the vehicle at the time. 3 NFL STARS HIT COMMISSIONER'S EXEMPT LIST AFTER OFFSEASON FILLED WITH LEGAL TROUBLE Police reported that the woman sustained multiple cuts and contusions from the shattered glass, and the infant, sitting in a baby seat, had glass found on his hair, face and car seat. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! When news of the arrest and subsequent charges surfaced in August, during the team's training camp, the Ravens stated they had been aware of the situation, were in direct communication with Bateman, notified the NFL office, and were cooperating with the league and authorities while treating it as a pending legal matter. The NFL opened a review of the matter but, meanwhile, the Ravens did not suspend, deactivate, or place Bateman on any disciplinary leave. And they still have not. Also, Baltimore's mayor did not release a statement about Bateman and domestic abuse. So the guy arrested on domestic abuse allegations has remained untouched so far. But the guy who said something arguably inappropriate (maybe) and apologized the next day, gets suspended one game "for now." The Baltimore Ravens have totally lost the plot. As the team gears up to face the Houston Texans in the next few hours, all eyes remain on the popular quarterback, Daniel Jones.Is Daniel Jones fit enough to take the field for the Indianapolis Colts as the team prepares to go against the Houston Texans?Yes, Daniel Jones is healthy and will start at quarterback for the Indianapolis Colts against the Houston Texans.According to the Indianapolis Colts’ recent injury report, starting offensive tackles Bernhard Raimann (concussion) and Jalen Travis (knee) are both sidelined alongside starting cornerback Charvarius Ward Sr. (knee), tight end Will Mallory (hamstring), and defensive tackle Jerry Tillery (calf).Popular cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf) is listed as questionable after missing all week of walkthroughs, with reports indicating that he is not expected to play.Apart from them, Anthony Gould (toe), backup tackle Charlie Heck (personal), and long snapper Luke Rhodes (hamstring) are all questionable, while linebacker Jaylon Carlies (neck) was placed on injured reserve earlier in the week.Daniel Jones’ poor performance sparks concern as the Indianapolis Colts struggle on the fieldAhead of Week 11’s clash against the Houston Texans, the 28 year old quarterback Daniel Jones leads the league in interceptions with 12 and has just seven touchdown passes.His completion percentage is 59.6 which has sparked major concern about why he has not been benched yet.A few hours ago, NFL insider ESPN's Jeremy Fowler noted in a recent report, "Colts head coach Shane Steichen's loyalty to Daniel Jones might be less about Jones' poor performance and more about the options behind him. As it was told to me, Steichen simply is not motivated to play Anthony Richardson Sr., the 2023 fourth overall pick who fell out of favor after a strong start to his rookie year. Richardson and No. 3 quarterback Riley Leonard did not have strong training camps in the Colts' view, and it seems that has carried over.”ESPN's Jeremy Fowler added, “Richardson, a 2027 free agent, badly needs a fresh start elsewhere but appears poised for spot duty in Indy at some point this year, given the team's 3-7 record and its trading away of four key players before the deadline. articles.title: 2 Small Studies Find a Clue in the Quest to Help Diagnose CTE in the Living
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — Scientists stumbled onto a hint that measuring a toxic protein tied to Alzheimer's disease just might one day be useful in diagnosing a different brain disease in football players and others who have suffered repeated blows to the head.
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Scientists stumbled onto a hint that measuring a toxic protein tied to Alzheimer's disease just might one day be useful in diagnosing a different brain disease in football players and others who have suffered repeated blows to the head.

Doctors evaluate symptoms such as mood swings and memory loss to try to tell if patients may have CTE, or chronic traumatic encephalopathy, a disease linked to concussions and other brain trauma. But other diseases cause similar symptoms, and a CTE diagnosis can only be confirmed by examining the brain after death.

Now two small studies are highlighting a new clue — that a blood test being developed to spot abnormal tau in the brains of Alzheimer's patients seems to also detect buildup of that protein in people with advanced CTE.

Tau normally supports neurons but in Alzheimer's, it tangles inside those nerve cells. Scientists are developing a blood test to track those tangles by detecting a particular tau fragment called eMTBR-tau243. But researchers at Washington University in St. Louis got a surprise when using autopsy records to study the new test – finding someone with high levels of that biomarker who didn't have Alzheimer's but CTE instead.

The researchers turned to a larger collection of autopsied brain and blood samples, eventually testing blood stored from 11 people classified as having CTE.

Compared to samples stored from healthy people, levels of eMTBR-tau243 were higher in those with advanced CTE, said study co-author Chihiro Sato, a WashU assistant neurology professor. That biomarker couldn't reliably identify early-stage CTE, the research team reported at a dementia meeting in Japan last week.

Separately, researchers at Boston University and Arizona's Banner Health were studying the same question using blood stored from 21 former professional or school football players who also donated their brain for research after death. Autopsies found 16 died with advanced CTE, two with earlier-stage CTE and three didn't have the disease.

Blood levels of that tau biomarker were significantly higher in the athletes with advanced CTE, the researchers reported Thursday at a scientific meeting in Boston. Adding to the complexity, five of those with CTE also had Alzheimer's disease, resulting in the highest levels of that tau biomarker.

Both studies were published in the medical journal JAMA.

The possible CTE link is interesting but very preliminary, requiring much larger studies to see if there's a real connection, cautioned Northwestern University neuropathologist Dr. Rudolph Castellani, who wasn't involved with the research.

Abnormal tau is found in several additional brain diseases, which can overlap in older adults. Moreover, tau buildup in CTE is different from the type that occurs in Alzheimer's, Drs. Günter Höglinger and Carla Palleis of Germany's Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich wrote in an accompanying editorial in the journal.

They also stressed the need for far more research, while saying the two studies together "represent an important step" in the quest to one day detect CTE in living patients.

articles.title: Joe Burrow va a ritmo de MVP y de firmar la mejor temporada de pases de la historia de la NFL
articles.standfirst: Los Bengals llevan una racha de cinco triunfos en los que el QB ha hecho al menos cuatro pases de touchdown
articles.summary: Los Bengals llevan una racha de cinco triunfos en los que el QB ha hecho al menos cuatro pases de touchdown
articles.body: Joe Burrow lleva varias semanas a ritmo de MVP y tras su partido ante los Pittsburgh Steelers es sin duda el claro favorito. El jugador de los Cincinnati Bengals lanzó para 409 yardas y cuatro touchdowns, completando casi el 80% de sus pases, y pudo haber elevado estos guarismos, pero fue cambiado. Su entrenador Zac Taylor no tiene dudas de que el nivel que está mostrando su QB es estratosférico. “Sería imposible afirmar que alguien está jugando mejor. No veo todos los partidos... pero apuesto a que quienes no hablan de él no ven nuestros partidos, porque si los vieran, sería muy difícil negar que es el mejor jugador del planeta", comentó Taylor. Todavía quedan ocho partidos para que acabe la temporada regular (el martes que viene visitan a los Commanders), pero Burrow, un ‘pocket passer’ de la vieja escuela, cumple todos los requisitos para ser MVP. Los Bengals comandan la AFC Norte con una marca de 7-2 y luego están sus estadísticas. Es uno de los cinco únicos quarterbacks en la historia de la NFL con más de 30 touchdowns en total en nueve partidos. Los otros cuatro ganaron el MVP y son: Tom Brady en 2007, Aaron Rodgers en 2011, Peyton Manning en 2013 y Patrick Mahomes en 2018. Burrow lleva 30 TD (27 de pase y 3 de carrera) con un porcentaje de pases completos de 74,7% (254/340) y un promedio de 310,6 yardas por partido. Los números tras nueve duelos del ganador del trofeo Heisman y campeón de NCAA en 2019, son mejores que cuando llevó a su franquicia a la Super Bowl en 2022: 22 TD, 70,0 % (233/333) y 281,7. Tras su último partido, Burrow se unió a Peyton Manning como los únicos dos quarterbacks con cinco encuentros consecutivos con al menos cuatro touchdowns. De hecho, los Bengals llevan una racha de cinco triunfos. Al QB le queda lo complicado, que es no bajar el ritmo, pero si no hay contratiempos llegaría al menos a 5.000 yardas y 50 touchdowns en una temporada. Eso sí, ¿alcanzará los 55 touchdowns de Manning en 2013?

articles.title: NFL analyst rips Marlon Humphrey over controversial Baltimore remarks
articles.summary: NFL analyst Douzable says Marlon Humphrey damaged his Baltimore legacy with his podcast comments.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey is facing criticism after his podcast comments about the city triggered a strong response from the NFL organization.

The Ravens sent Humphrey home from practice and made him inactive for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers. His remarks also drew criticism from Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott.

Speaking on NFL on CBS, former NFL defensive lineman Leger Douzable questioned Humphrey's judgment and the impact of his comments.

"First and foremost… was drafted in the first round for the Baltimore Ravens," Douzable said. "Legacy is something that players, we all think about while we're playing, whether people want to admit it or not. He's tarnished his legacy in Baltimore with this comment."

"Now, you're on your podcast. You may have been kidding around, but you don't kid around with stuff like this."

Humphrey sparked the controversy during an episode of The Marlon Humphrey Show. Asked what Baltimore was best at making, he joked, "They're best at making criminals."

Douzable called the remark "insane" and "asinine," pointing to Humphrey's connection with the city and its supporters.

"There's so many kids in that community that look up to you," he said. "As professional athletes, we have a duty to the communities that we play in… He's always been a guy that's interacted with the fans, and for you to say this just makes absolutely no sense."

Marlon Humphrey controversy creates another problem

Humphrey later apologized to reporters, but Douzable questioned whether the response showed enough regret. Douzable said Humphrey's apology appeared half-hearted. He also warned that the situation could affect the cornerback's future in Baltimore.

"It was like he didn't even really want to apologize," Douzable said.

The analyst also compared the situation to C.J. Gardner-Johnson's departure from Buffalo. He suggested the Ravens could eventually release Humphrey after initially making him inactive.

"There's players gonna miss games because of injury," Douzable said. "They've already essentially made him inactive for this game coming up. And truth be told, I can see this playing out like C.J. Garner-Johnson, where the Bills kept him for a week and then released him.

"And this just sucks for the legacy that you built in Baltimore because these comments made absolutely no sense."

The controversy comes during a difficult season for Baltimore. The Ravens sit at 4-6 after five consecutive losses. Humphrey has spent his entire NFL career with Baltimore since the team selected him 16th overall in 2017. He has earned three Pro Bowl selections and first-team All-Pro honors.

Humphrey's comments have now created a major distraction for a struggling team. How Baltimore handles the situation could determine whether Humphrey has a future with the franchise.

articles.title: Bills vs. Dolphins: 5 things to watch for during Week 11's game
articles.summary: Here are five things to watch for on the field between the Bills and Dolphins in Week 11.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills will roll on with their 2026 NFL regular season on Sunday with their next game en route against the Miami Dolphins . Kickoff from Highmark Stadium will take place at 1 p.m.

The Dolphins head to western New York in dire need of a win. Miami sits at 1-8 and hope to rebuild their franchise's culture. But some Dolphins fans are already in "tanking" mode.

Between two such teams in the Bills and Dolphins, what should you keep in mind during the contest?

With that, here are Bills Wire's five things to watch for in Week 11 :

The Bills are massive favorites. It's hard to exactly judge or know Buffalo's team is actively overlooking the Dolphins on Sunday... but if they do, you'll know it.

The Bills are a huge 16.5-point favorite. A win still have to be delivered and the Dolphins do have a surprisingly good defense that is ranked 10th in the NFL (320.6 YPG) and this is the NFL. We've seen crazy before. The Bills have to avoid that at all costs.

One way the Bills could do exactly that is by starting games quicker. That has not always been the case this season. Look no further than last week. Buffalo held a slight lead on the New York Jets at halftime before blowing them out in the second half in a 31-12 final .

The Bills will want to get in their groove early in games before the postseason as well.

While the Bills should not overlook the Dolphins, we're allowed to do that as onlookers.

There is a bit of a hope that the likes of Kyle Allen and other Bills backups get in this game in the second half. That would mean Buffalo is winning big and that would give their starters a bit of a break ahead of a short week. The Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving Day on Thursday. Fresher players for that one would be nice.

One injury being watched in Buffalo is the wrist issue No. 1 cornerback Christian Benford has played with. Benford has missed practice time this week because of that injury.

The Bills win over the Jets was a bit of a breakout game for TJ Parker.

Parker, Buffalo's top rookie draft pick , recorded five tackles, including two for loss, with two sacks. He was the Bills' pass rusher that stood out the most on their defense.

Did Parker earn more playing time against the Dolphins over the likes of someone like Bradley Chubb?

articles.title: Rams’ Puka Nacua suspended for violating NFL’s personal conduct policy
articles.summary: The NFL is suspending Puka Nacua for three games.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua has reportedly been suspended by the NFL.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Nacua is being suspended for three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy.

However, players can serve out suspensions while on injured reserve, which Nacua currently is, so he's not going to miss any games.

"ESPN sources: NFL is suspending Rams standout WR Puka Nacua three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy," Schefter reported. "The suspension is effective immediately and he is eligible for reinstatement Monday Dec. 14. Players may serve suspensions while on injured reserve, which he is."

Nacua's suspension likely stems from his being named in a civil lawsuit during the offseason.

While he won't miss any games as a result of the suspension, Nacua will lose three game checks worth of money. That comes out to a total of $961,167.

But that dollar amount pales in comparison to what it would have been if Nacua had served his suspension next season, when he's going to be playing on a more lucrative contract.

A 2023 fifth-round pick, Nacua is slated to be a free agent in 2027 and should get paid as one of the best wide receivers in the NFL.

Nacua landed on injured reserve last week because of knee and toe injuries.

He is eligible to be activated after three more games, although the expectation is he'll need more time than that.

Nacua's specific injuries are MCL and PCL sprains in his knee, and turf toe, all of which he suffered near the end of the Week 9 game against the Washington Commanders.

articles.title: Rams All-Pro WR Puka Nacua reportedly suspended 3 games for violating league's personal conduct policy
articles.summary: Nacua is currently on injured reserve with knee and toe injuries.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua has reportedly been suspended for three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Thursday.

Nacua's suspension will go into effect immediately, and he will be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, Dec. 14, Schefter added. The All-Pro wideout is currently on injured reserve with knee and turf toe injuries sustained in Week 9's win over the Washington Commanders.

The end of his suspension coincides with his potential timeline to return from injured reserve, though head coach Sean McVay noted he is expected to miss "significant time." Still, if he were to be healthy by that point, he would not need to miss any additional time due to the suspension.

Nacua's suspension stems from a roller coaster of an offseason, as he faced a civil lawsuit from a woman over an alleged biting incident and antisemitic comments earlier this year. An attorney representing Nacua denied the woman's claim that he made the antisemitic comment while downplaying the bite mark he left on her.

His attorney soon after confirmed that Nacua entered a holistic care facility after facing the off-field allegations.

Upon his return to the team for OTAs, Nacua declined to comment on the situation specifically, citing ongoing legal matters, but he acknowledged this time as "a moment for me to learn from some of the situations I was putting myself in and then also having just an awareness of how I'm conducting myself in and out of this football field."
